title: Open-Source Media and Marketing Mix Modeling: Practice-Oriented Overview, Challenges, Opportunities
author_source: Julian Runge & Koen Pauwels, Customer Needs and Solutions, 2026, review article (also MSI Working Paper 26-106, March 2026)
note: The best single overview of the course topic: a narrative review comparing Meta Robyn, Google Meridian/LightweightMMM and the PyMC-Labs ecosystem (PyMC-Marketing). Frames the 2020s MMM revival as a response to privacy-enhancing technologies (ATT, cookie loss) and warns that automation can hide misspecification, too little variation in spend, and endogeneity. It recommends calibrating with experiments. Gives no explicit multi-country treatment, so pair it with the geo-hierarchical papers.
course_use: reading (session 1 anchor); journal version paid / WU-Lizenz prüfen, MSI working-paper PDF free (see reports row)

title: Media Mix Model Calibration With Bayesian Priors
author_source: Yingxiang Zhang, Mike Wurm, Eddie Li, Alexander Wakim, Joseph Kelly, Brenda Price, Ying Liu; Google, 2024, technical paper
note: The methodological core of Meridian's ROI priors. It reparameterises the MMM so that ROAS is a model parameter, which lets lift or geo-experiment results enter the model directly as a prior. Simulations show this reduces bias and uncertainty. Useful for teaching how a country team's local lift test becomes that market's prior. Short and readable for master students who know basic Bayes.
course_use: reading / lab (set ROI priors in Meridian); free PDF

title: Bias Correction for Paid Search in Media Mix Modeling
author_source: Aiyou Chen, David Chan, Mike Perry, Yuxue Jin, Yunting Sun, Yueqing Wang, Jim Koehler; Google, 2018, technical paper (arXiv 1807.03292)
note: Uses causal diagrams (back-door criterion) to explain why paid-search ROAS is biased upward in MMM: search ads are targeted at existing demand. Proposes controlling for search query volume. This is the origin of Meridian's Google Query Volume control. The search-demand argument also matters across countries, because Google's search share differs strongly between markets (it is low in China, Korea and Russia).
course_use: reading (causal MMM session); free

title: A Primer on Out-of-the-Box AI Marketing Mix Models
author_source: Macarena Estévez, María Teresa Ballestar, Jorge Sáinz; IEEE Transactions on Engineering Management 72, 282-294, 2025
note: Fits a traditional econometric MMM and Meta Robyn to the same telecom dataset from a European (Spanish) firm, then compares them on technical, business and practical criteria. A clear case for a 'traditional vs automated' debate. Main caveat: Robyn's random initialisation and Pareto front of candidate models make results harder to replicate and explain.
course_use: reading / class discussion; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Marketing Mix Modeling in Lemonade
author_source: Roy Ravid, arXiv 2501.01276, 2025, industry case paper
note: A short end-to-end account of how a digital insurer built an in-house Bayesian MMM: seasonality, trend and macro controls, validation against A/B tests and sliding-window holdouts, then budget reallocation by convex optimisation. Good as a template for student project reports. It covers one company and does not name the software used.
course_use: reading / project template; open access

title: Structural Estimation of Marketing Mix Model Parameters from Geo-Experiments
author_source: Niklas Heusch, arXiv 2608.21128, 2026, methods preprint
note: Recovers adstock decay, saturation and effectiveness parameters directly from treated-vs-control geo-experiment time series, then pools several experiments to calibrate an MMM. This connects to the multi-market question of how geo tests run in a few countries can inform a global model. Demonstrated only on synthetic data; a very recent preprint, not peer reviewed.
course_use: background / advanced reading; open access

title: A Synthetic Benchmark Dataset with Endogenous Marketing Spend for Validating Marketing Mix Models
author_source: Niklas Heusch, arXiv 2608.21130, 2026, data/methods preprint
note: Provides simulated data with known ground truth in which budgets respond to demand, the realistic case that standard simulators leave out. Lets students check whether Robyn, Meridian or PyMC-Marketing recover the true ROAS when spend is endogenous. Preprint; check that the data repository is available before you assign it.
course_use: lab (tool comparison against ground truth); open access

title: PyMC: A Modern and Comprehensive Probabilistic Programming Framework in Python
author_source: Oriol Abril-Pla, Virgile Andreani, Colin Carroll, Larry Dong, Christopher Fonnesbeck et al.; PeerJ Computer Science 9:e1516, 2023
note: The citable reference for the inference engine underneath PyMC-Marketing: NUTS sampling, model graphs, the ArviZ diagnostics workflow. Read it for the background behind convergence checks (r-hat, divergences) that students meet in PyMC-Marketing labs. Software paper, not marketing.
course_use: background for lab; open access

title: Bayesian Workflow
author_source: Andrew Gelman, Aki Vehtari, Daniel Simpson et al., arXiv 2011.01808, 2020
note: The standard reference for the prior-predictive, fit, posterior-predictive and model-comparison loop that PyMC-Marketing's documentation follows. Gives students a vocabulary for judging any Bayesian MMM, including country-level ones. Long (77 pp.); assign sections 2-6.
course_use: reading (selected sections) / lab guide; open access

title: TensorFlow Distributions
author_source: Joshua V. Dillon, Ian Langmore, Dustin Tran, Eugene Brevdo et al., arXiv 1711.10604, 2017
note: Meridian runs on TensorFlow Probability; its predecessor LightweightMMM used NumPyro/JAX. Optional background for students who want to know why Meridian needs a GPU or long MCMC runs for many geos. Technical; instructor reference only.
course_use: background (instructor); open access

title: Forecasting at Scale (Prophet)
author_source: Sean J. Taylor & Benjamin Letham; The American Statistician 72(1), 37-45, 2018
note: Robyn uses Prophet to break the baseline into trend, seasonality and holidays, using country-specific holiday calendars, which matters in multi-country work. The paper explains the additive model behind that step, so students can see what Robyn's 'prophet_country' argument actually does.
course_use: background for Robyn lab; open access

title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems
author_source: Arthur E. Hoerl & Robert W. Kennard; Technometrics 12(1), 55-67, 1970
note: The original ridge paper. Robyn is a ridge regression with Nevergrad hyperparameter search, used against collinear media spends. Contrasting ridge shrinkage with Bayesian priors (Meridian, PyMC-Marketing) is a good exam question. Classic, short.
course_use: background; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Ghost Ads: Improving the Economics of Measuring Online Ad Effectiveness
author_source: Garrett A. Johnson, Randall A. Lewis, Elmar I. Nubbemeyer; Journal of Marketing Research 54(6), 867-884, 2017
note: Explains how platform lift studies (the 'conversion lift' inputs to Robyn and Meridian calibration) create valid control groups. Helps students judge what a Meta or Google lift result does and does not measure before using it as an MMM prior.
course_use: reading (calibration session); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Cross-National Differences in Market Response: Line-Length, Price, and Distribution Elasticities in 14 Indo-Pacific Rim Economies
author_source: Hannes Datta, Harald J. van Heerde, Marnik G. Dekimpe, Jan-Benedict E.M. Steenkamp; Journal of Marketing Research 59(2), 251-270, 2022
note: Covers more than 1,600 brands in 14 categories across 7 developed and 7 emerging economies, using GfK data from 2004-2014. Average elasticities: price -0.42, distribution 0.37, line length 0.46. It finds no systematic emerging-vs-developed gap; power distance and income inequality explain most cross-country differences. Directly useful for choosing country-level priors and for arguing for partial pooling across markets. A replication package is on SAGE figshare, but the raw data are not included.
course_use: core reading (international session); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: An Investigation into the Evolution of Marketing-Mix Effectiveness: An Empirics-First Approach
author_source: Katrijn Gielens & Jan-Benedict E.M. Steenkamp; Journal of Marketing, 2025
note: Household-panel evidence on more than 16,000 brands in 85 CPG categories across 34 countries. Gives time-varying price (-0.64), assortment (0.31) and distribution (0.21) elasticities, and finds 98.5% of brands show significant drift. Arguments for time-varying coefficients and for refreshing country MMMs. Local vs global brand status matters for those trajectories.
course_use: reading / benchmark priors; open access per OpenAlex

title: In Brands We Trust? A Multicategory, Multicountry Investigation of Sensitivity of Consumers' Trust in Brands to Marketing-Mix Activities
author_source: Koushyar Rajavi, Tarun Kushwaha, Jan-Benedict E.M. Steenkamp; Journal of Consumer Research 46(4), 2019
note: Combines a 15,073-respondent survey with scanner data on 589 brands in 13 countries. Advertising raises brand trust, and that effect is moderated by national cultural values. Useful for discussing long-term brand effects that a weekly sales MMM misses and that differ by country.
course_use: background reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Understanding the Coevolution of Ad Spend by Media Channel and Retail Format Sales at the Country Level: A Multicountry Examination
author_source: Hannah S. Lee, Göksel Yalcinkaya, David A. Griffith; Journal of International Marketing, 2023 (online 2022)
note: A 29-country panel showing large cross-country differences in which media channels matter and how they move with retail formats. Supports the 'glocal' argument that one global media mix cannot be assumed. Use it to motivate country-specific channel sets in a geo-hierarchical MMM.
course_use: reading (international session); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: New Empirical Generalizations on the Determinants of Price Elasticity
author_source: Tammo H.A. Bijmolt, Harald J. van Heerde, Rik G.M. Pieters; Journal of Marketing Research 42(2), 141-156, 2005
note: Meta-analysis of 1,851 price elasticities (mean about -2.6), with moderators including Europe vs the US. A source of informative priors for price and promotion terms in an MMM, and a reminder that price-level and currency effects differ by market.
course_use: background (priors); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Manufacturer and Retailer Strategies to Impact Store Brand Share: Global Integration, Local Adaptation, and Worldwide Learning
author_source: Jan-Benedict E.M. Steenkamp & Inge Geyskens; Marketing Science 33(1), 2014 (online 2013)
note: Multi-country study framed around global integration, local adaptation and worldwide learning. A good conceptual mapping to complete pooling, no pooling and partial pooling in hierarchical MMM. Helps international-marketing students see why Bayesian shrinkage across countries is a strategic as well as a statistical choice.
course_use: background / conceptual bridge; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Privacy Regulation and Online Advertising
author_source: Avi Goldfarb & Catherine E. Tucker; Management Science 57(1), 57-71, 2011
note: A classic cross-country design: after the EU ePrivacy rules, display ads became about 65% less effective at changing purchase intent compared with non-EU countries. An early example of regulation creating country differences in measurability and ad effectiveness.
course_use: reading (privacy session); open access version available

title: Regulating Privacy Online: An Economic Evaluation of the GDPR
author_source: Samuel G. Goldberg, Garrett A. Johnson, Scott K. Shriver; American Economic Journal: Economic Policy 16(1), 2024
note: Adobe Analytics data for 1,084 firms show about 12% lower recorded EU pageviews and revenue after the GDPR. The authors split this into lost data recording versus real effects. That split is the key point for MMM teaching: user-level attribution loses observability in the EU, while aggregate MMM inputs do not.
course_use: reading (privacy session); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Privacy and Market Concentration: Intended and Unintended Consequences of the GDPR
author_source: Garrett A. Johnson, Scott K. Shriver, Samuel G. Goldberg; Management Science 69(10), 2023
note: Covers 27,000+ websites: EU vendor use fell 15% and vendor concentration rose 17%, in favour of Google and Facebook. Context for why platform-supplied open-source MMMs (Meridian, Robyn) reached the market and for the neutrality question they raise.
course_use: background; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Impact of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) on Online Tracking
author_source: Klaus M. Miller, Karlo Lukic, Bernd Skiera; International Journal of Research in Marketing, 2025
note: European authors. A difference-in-differences study of 294 publishers finds about 4 fewer trackers per site (-14.8%) because of the GDPR, but only limited effects on advertising trackers. A nuanced counterpoint to the 'GDPR killed attribution' story.
course_use: reading; open access

title: Evaluating the Impact of Privacy Regulation on E-Commerce Firms: Evidence from Apple's App Tracking Transparency
author_source: Guy Aridor, Yeon-Koo Che, Brett Hollenbeck, Maximilian Kaiser, Daniel McCarthy; Management Science, 2025
note: Covers more than 4,200 e-commerce advertisers: click-through rates on Meta conversion ads fell 37% after ATT; spend shifted to Google; revenue of Meta-dependent firms fell 8-40%, mostly at small firms. The clearest causal evidence for the signal loss behind Meta's investment in Robyn. Co-author Kaiser is at Universität Hamburg, and the findings fed into German and French competition cases.
course_use: core reading (why MMM now); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen; MSI WP version free

title: Estimating the Value of Offsite Tracking Data to Advertisers: Evidence from Meta
author_source: Nils Wernerfelt, Anna Tuchman, Bradley T. Shapiro, Robert Moakler; Marketing Science 44(2), 268-286, 2025
note: A randomized experiment with more than 70,000 advertisers: losing offsite (pixel/SDK) data raises the median cost per incremental customer by 31%, and hits small advertisers hardest. Quantifies what attribution loses under ATT/GDPR-type restrictions. Two authors were Meta employees, which is worth discussing.
course_use: reading (privacy session); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen; NBER WP w32765 free

title: Measuring Digital Advertising in a Post-Cookie Era: A Study of Marketing-Mix Models, Attribution and Incrementality
author_source: Shashank Hosahally, Madan Bharadwaj, Arkadiusz Zaremba, Olena Volkova; Journal of Digital & Social Media Marketing, 2025
note: A practitioner-journal piece framed explicitly around EU GDPR. Compares MMM, attribution and incrementality testing as complementary tools once cookies and fingerprinting are restricted. Accessible for students without econometric training; lighter on evidence than the academic papers.
course_use: reading (practitioner view); open access per OpenAlex

title: Statistical Rethinking: A Bayesian Course with Examples in R and Stan (2nd ed.)
author_source: Richard McElreath, CRC Press / Chapman & Hall, 2020, textbook
note: Chapters 13-14 (multilevel models, partial pooling, varying slopes) are the most intuitive introduction to why a geo- or country-hierarchical MMM shrinks small markets toward the global mean. Free lecture videos and PyMC ports of all examples exist, so it fits a Python lab.
course_use: background reading for the hierarchical session; book paid (~EUR 70), lectures and code free

title: Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd ed.)
author_source: Andrew Gelman, John Carlin, Hal Stern, David Dunson, Aki Vehtari, Donald Rubin; CRC Press, 2013
note: The reference text. Chapter 5 (hierarchical models, the eight-schools example) maps directly onto 'eight countries with noisy ROAS'. The authors have made the PDF freely available for non-commercial use. For instructors and advanced students.
course_use: instructor reference / advanced reading; free PDF

title: Regression and Other Stories
author_source: Andrew Gelman, Jennifer Hill, Aki Vehtari; Cambridge University Press, 2020
note: Applied regression with a Bayesian slant: priors, simulation, causal inference chapters. A gentle path for marketing master students before PyMC-Marketing. A free PDF and all code are on the companion site.
course_use: background reading; free PDF

title: Bayesian Statistics and Marketing
author_source: Peter E. Rossi, Greg M. Allenby, Robert McCulloch; Wiley, 2005
note: The marketing-specific source for hierarchical Bayes models (unit-level heterogeneity, hierarchical linear models) behind cross-market pooling. Notation is dense and the code is in R (bayesm). Use selected chapters only.
course_use: instructor reference; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: R for Marketing Research and Analytics (2nd ed.)
author_source: Chris Chapman & Elea McDonnell Feit; Springer (Use R!), 2019
note: Robyn is an R package. This book gets students fluent in R data handling, and its hierarchical-Bayes chapter covers multilevel models. Complements the Python companion that is already on the list. Springer eBook, likely in the WU package.
course_use: lab support for the Robyn track; WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink)

title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, Ya Xu; Cambridge University Press, 2020
note: Experiments are the calibration input for all three tools. Chapters on validity threats, sample-ratio mismatch and long-term effects help students judge the lift tests fed into Robyn, Meridian or PyMC-Marketing. Practitioner-oriented.
course_use: background (calibration session); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Global Brand Strategy: World-wise Marketing in the Age of Branding
author_source: Jan-Benedict E.M. Steenkamp; Palgrave Macmillan, 2017
note: Connects global vs local brand management, standardisation vs adaptation, and emerging vs developed markets to market-response evidence. Gives the international-marketing framing for why a global MMM must allow country-specific effects.
course_use: background reading (international framing); WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Controlling des Marketing Mix mit Marketing Mix Modeling (chapter in: Marketingcontrolling kompakt)
author_source: Sven Reinecke & Alexander Tombach; Springer Fachmedien Wiesbaden, 2025, book chapter (German)
note: German-language introduction to MMM for marketing controlling, by St. Gallen authors. Reports from a 2024 executive survey that about 25% of companies in the DACH region use MMM regularly. The best German entry text for students and for linking MMM to the controlling or finance function.
course_use: reading (German); WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink)

title: MSI Blue Ribbon Panel Report: Charting the Future of Marketing Mix Modeling Best Practices
author_source: Marketing Science Institute (Arora, Berman, Feit, Hanssens, Li, Lovett, Mela, Wilbur, Lynch), 2023, white paper
note: An academic panel's best-practice statement on MMM, written in response to privacy-driven signal loss: what MMM is used for (proving contribution, forecasting, optimisation), the challenges, and how to judge vendor claims. Useful for setting quality criteria for student projects. Only the preview is free; the full report needs MSI membership.
course_use: background reading; preview free, full report members only (check WU MSI access)

title: Open-Source Media and Marketing Mix Modeling (MSI Working Paper 26-106)
author_source: Julian Runge & Koen Pauwels, Marketing Science Institute / ARF, March 2026
note: Free working-paper version of the Customer Needs and Solutions review (see articles). Listed here because WU students can read the MSI PDF without a journal licence. Compares Robyn, Meridian and PyMC-Marketing, with warnings about misspecification and endogeneity.
course_use: reading; free PDF (registration may be required)

title: Econometrics Explained 2
author_source: Louise Cook, IPA (Institute of Practitioners in Advertising, UK), 2017, guide
note: A non-technical guide to commissioning and reading MMM: what econometrics can and cannot do, how to plan an analysis, how to read the outputs, with IPA Effectiveness Awards cases. Good for students in client or brand-manager roles who have to brief and challenge a modeller. UK/European agency perspective.
course_use: reading (manager perspective); PDF download on IPA site (check access)

title: Marketing Mix Modeling Guidebook
author_source: Hakuhodo DY Media Partners (Japan), published via Think with Google, 2023
note: A long practitioner guidebook from a Japanese media agency: measurement challenges, model structure, parameter estimation, validation, use in decisions. Brings a non-Western market perspective to a mostly US/UK literature, which helps in comparing MMM practice across markets. Very large PDF (>10 MB).
course_use: reading / project reference; free

title: Meridian marketing mix model (Think with Google article, German edition: Meridian Marketing-Mix-Modell)
author_source: Google, Think with Google / business.google.com, 2025
note: Google's launch article for Meridian (general availability January 2025), in German, with FR, ES, IT, UK and APAC editions. Explains calibration with experiments, reach and frequency, and geo-level modelling for marketers. Comparing the localised editions is a small exercise in how one tool is marketed globally. Vendor source, so not neutral.
course_use: background (vendor view); free

title: Marketing Mix Model: The Opportunities Behind Open-Source Techniques
author_source: Deloitte España, 22 February 2024, consulting perspective (English text)
note: A short consultancy view on open-source MMM: cost, community and flexibility vs limited support, integration effort and the need for an in-house analytics team. Frames in-house vs outsourced vs hybrid operating models. A European consultancy view useful for 'build vs buy' discussions. Light on evidence.
course_use: class discussion (operating model); free

title: 2025 Annual Marketing Report (From Chaos to Clarity)
author_source: Nielsen, May 2025, global survey report (1,400 senior marketers)
note: Global marketer survey with regional splits, e.g. Europe vs APAC on budget cuts and on confidence in measuring ROI. Nielsen's 2025 ROI findings show that few marketers measure traditional and digital media holistically. Gives students cross-regional context on measurement maturity. Vendor report; download is gated by a form.
course_use: background data for project motivation; free (registration)

title: Cross-Media Measurement (Halo framework and North Star principles)
author_source: World Federation of Advertisers (WFA), 2019-2025, programme pages and reports
note: The global advertiser body's privacy-safe cross-media reach and frequency framework. It is rolled out market by market (UK Origin with ISBA, US Aquila with ANA). Shows how multinational advertisers organise measurement country by country, and supplies the reach and frequency inputs that Meridian can use. Some documents are WFA members only.
course_use: background (multi-market measurement governance); partly free, partly login

title: The Long and the Short of It: Balancing Short and Long-Term Marketing Strategies
author_source: Les Binet & Peter Field, IPA, 2013, effectiveness report
note: Based on the IPA Effectiveness Databank. Argues that weekly sales MMMs capture short-term activation but underestimate brand-building effects (the often-cited 60:40 brand/activation split). A caveat to discuss for all three tools, whose adstock windows are short. UK-centric data.
course_use: reading (limits of MMM); paid / IPA members (summary materials widely available)

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
author_source: European Parliament and Council, Official Journal of the EU, 2016
note: Primary legal source for the privacy argument behind MMM adoption in Europe. Articles 6-7 (lawful basis, consent) explain why user-level tracking became consent-dependent in the EU. Aggregate, non-personal MMM data generally fall outside its scope, which is worth discussing with students. Available in German (DSGVO) and all EU languages.
course_use: background (privacy session); free

title: User Privacy and Data Use (App Tracking Transparency)
author_source: Apple Inc., App Store developer guidelines, since iOS 14.5 (2021)
note: Apple's official description of the ATT opt-in requirement for cross-app tracking. Pair it with the Aridor et al. and Wernerfelt et al. papers to show the platform-policy, not legal, source of signal loss. ATT applies globally, while GDPR applies only in the EU: a useful contrast for international marketing.
course_use: background (privacy session); free

title: PyMC-Marketing Example Gallery (MMM notebooks)
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2026, official docs (notebook gallery)
note: Central index of all MMM notebooks, grouped by theme: multidimensional/geo (Multidimensional Example, Custom Geo-Hierarchical MMM with Splines, Halo and Cannibalisation in Multi-Dimensional MMMs, Funnel-Aware Geo-Level Mediation), budget allocation (incl. risk assessment, multi-objective, Pareto across products with a shared budget), lift-test calibration (incl. geo-level lift tests), time-varying parameters, two end-to-end case studies. Good map for picking lab notebooks. Content tracks the latest release (1.x), so pin the version for a course.
course_use: reading / lab preparation (instructor picks notebooks); free

title: MMM Multidimensional Example Notebook (Geo-MMM)
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2025-2026, official docs (notebook)
note: Key notebook for multi-market teaching: simulated weekly sales for two markets (geo_a, geo_b), 2 channels, 2 event controls, built with dims=("geo",) and target scaled per geo. Shows mixed pooling choices in one model: hierarchical saturation beta per channel x geo (non-centred), fully pooled lambda, unpooled adstock alpha, geo-specific intercepts and Fourier seasonality. Explains full vs no vs partial pooling and recommends adding complexity step by step; prior predictive check, sampling diagnostics, budget optimisation per geo. Since v1.0 this multidimensional class IS the default MMM.
course_use: lab (core multi-country exercise: swap geos for countries); free

title: Custom Geo-Hierarchical MMM with Splines
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2025-2026, official docs (notebook)
note: Shows how to build a custom hierarchical geo model by combining PyMC-Marketing components (adstock, saturation) with plain PyMC: each geo gets its own spline weights for the baseline, with shared hyperpriors. Useful to show students what happens 'under the hood' and to compare with Meridian's spline/knot baseline.
course_use: lab (advanced, optional); free

title: MMM Calibration with Geo-Level Lift Tests
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2026, official docs (notebook)
note: Simulates 8 geos x 104 weeks; 4 treated geos get extra spend for 8 weeks with 4 paired controls. Estimates per-geo lift, then fits an uncalibrated and a calibrated hierarchical MMM. Saturation parameters use (geo, channel) dims with channel-level hyperpriors, so evidence from treated geos informs control geos via partial pooling. Result: narrower mROAS intervals, closer to truth in 3 of 4 geos. Ideal for teaching 'test in a few countries, borrow strength for the rest'.
course_use: lab / homework; free

title: Halo and Cannibalisation Effects in Multi-Dimensional MMMs
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2026, official docs (notebook)
note: Multi-dimensional MMM where spend in one dimension (product/brand/market) can lift or cannibalise another. Good discussion starter for cross-market spillovers (e.g. German TV spilling into Austria) and portfolio brands.
course_use: reading / advanced lab; free

title: Multi-Objective Optimization and Pareto Optimization Across Products with a Shared Media Budget
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2026, official docs (notebooks)
note: Shows how to merge several fitted models into one optimiser and trade off objectives; the companion notebook mmm_pareto_optimization.html allocates one media budget across products. Directly transferable to allocating a central (HQ) budget across country models.
course_use: lab (budget allocation across markets); free

title: Why and how to account for media inflation in your MMM
author_source: PyMC Labs, pymc-marketing.io, 2026, official docs (notebook)
note: Explains why rising media prices distort spend-based effects and how to adjust. Relevant for international data where CPMs, inflation and currency movements differ by country; pair with the cost-per-unit notebook (mmm_cost_per_unit.html). None of the three tools has a built-in FX conversion, so this is the closest official guidance.
course_use: reading / discussion (currency and price differences across markets); free

author_source: PyMC Labs, GitHub releases, August 2026, release notes
note: States 'Multidimensional MMM is now the MMM': geo, product and channel dims first-class, one xr.Dataset for all inputs; about 1.5x faster sampling; PyMC 6 / ArviZ 1.2 stack; new plotting API. note: Curated list of videos (Wiecki, Bolt, yearly catch-up), business cases (Bolt, Shell and Databricks, HelloFresh), and third-party blogs (Orduz, Kübler, O'Sullivan on multicollinearity), plus the JellyPop tutorial repo and the MMM Explainer Streamlit app. Fast way to build a reading list; most entries are undated.

author_source: pymc-labs, GitHub Discussions, Feb-Mar 2025, community Q&A
note: Short thread showing how geo-hierarchical support entered the library (maintainer W. Dean points to the new multidimensional MMM, later the official notebook). Useful to show students how fast these tools change and how to read issues/discussions.

author_source: PyMC Discourse community, Feb 2025, forum thread
note: Practitioner with 4 geos x 5 channels asks how to report per-geo and overall contributions, saturation curves and budget allocation; answers explain slicing xarray contributions by geo, plotting curves with actual spend, custom optimisers for hierarchies and back-transforming scaled data. Links further geo threads (2023-2025).

title: Meridian documentation: About the project and full docs navigation
author_source: Google, developers.google.com, 2025-2026, official docs
note: Entry point to the three-stage workflow (pre-modeling, modeling, post-modeling) with links to loading geo-level data (with or without reach and frequency, organic media), national data, priors (ROI/mROI/contribution parameterisations, default priors, non-revenue KPI), calibration, optimisation scenarios and Scenario Planner. Its main purpose is calibrating Meridian. Install with pip install meridian-geox or pip install 'google-meridian[meridian-geox]'. Python 3.10+ (3.11+ with Meridian). Includes a Getting Started Colab and single- and multi-cell Colabs. Docs: https://developers.google.com/meridian/geox/install-geox
course_use: Lab or project: design a regional test, then feed the lift into the MMM; free

title: Robyn 3.12.1 (CRAN)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science; CRAN; v3.12.1 published 2 Jul 2025; MIT; R package
note: Meta's MMM: ridge regression, Nevergrad multi-objective hyperparameter search, Prophet decomposition, Pareto-front model selection with clustering, and a budget allocator. Requires R 4.0.0+; imports reticulate and prophet. Nevergrad (Python) must be set up once via reticulate (see demo/install_nevergrad.R). Install with install.packages("Robyn") or remotes::install_github("facebookexperimental/Robyn/R"). The GitHub repo has about 1.5k stars. A plumber-based Robyn API for Python has been in beta since Nov 2023.
course_use: Main R lab tool, good comparison with the Bayesian tools; free, open licence

title: Robyn Python port (robynpy 0.3.6, beta)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science; PyPI robynpy and GitHub Robyn/python folder; v0.3.6 released 3 Apr 2025; MIT; Python package (beta)
note: Native object-oriented Python rewrite of Robyn R version 3.11.1. Still needs R plus the glmnet R package. Install with pip install robynpy (Python 3.8+). It is a beta and translation issues from R may remain. Note that the PyPI package 'robyn' is an unrelated web framework.
course_use: Optional for Python-only students; free. Warn students about beta status

title: Robyn demo script (demo.R)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science; GitHub facebookexperimental/Robyn; R script; MIT
note: End-to-end walkthrough: loads dt_simulated_weekly and dt_prophet_holidays, sets prophet_country = "DE", defines paid media, organic and context variables, hyperparameters, calibration input, model selection and budget allocation. Changing the country code shows how holiday effects differ by country.
course_use: Step-by-step R lab script; free

title: siMMMulator: simulated data for MMM with known ground truth
author_source: Meta (facebookexperimental); GitHub; MIT; R package
note: Generates synthetic MMM datasets from scratch (baseline, channels, adstock, saturation, noise) with a known true ROI, so students can test whether Robyn, Meridian or PyMC-Marketing recover the truth. Has about 65 stars and no formal releases.
course_use: Homework: simulate several markets with different true ROIs and compare tools; free

title: AMSS: Aggregate Marketing System Simulator (R)
author_source: Google; GitHub google/amss; v1.0.1; Apache-2.0; R package; archived 7 Sep 2022
note: Simulates aggregate marketing time series with ground-truth metrics (Zhang and Vaver 2017). Archived and read-only, so use it only for illustration; siMMMulator or the Meridian simulated data are the maintained options.
course_use: Instructor background or optional simulation; free

title: GeoLift (R)
author_source: Meta (facebookincubator); GitHub; MIT; R package (R 4.0.0+); project status active
note: Geo experiments with augmented synthetic control: data-driven market selection, power calculators, multi-cell tests, commuting zones (vignettes). Gives lift estimates you can feed into Robyn calibration. Has about 271 stars.
course_use: Lab: pick test markets and estimate lift; free

title: CausalPy 0.9.0 (synthetic control, geo lift, DiD, ITS)
author_source: PyMC Labs; PyPI/GitHub; v0.9.0 released 28 Jul 2026 (1.0.0rc1 pre-release 6 Oct 2026); Apache-2.0; Python package
note: Bayesian (PyMC) and OLS quasi-experimental methods: synthetic control, geographical lift, difference-in-differences, interrupted time series. Python 3.12+. Install with pip install CausalPy or from conda-forge. Has about 1.2k stars. It pairs with PyMC-Marketing lift-test calibration.
course_use: Lab: estimate the lift of a country-level campaign; free

title: tfp-causalimpact (Python CausalImpact)
author_source: Google; GitHub google/tfp-causalimpact; Apache-2.0; Python package (TensorFlow Probability)
note: Python/TFP version of the Bayesian structural time-series CausalImpact method for the effect of an intervention on a time series. Install with pip install tfp-causalimpact; import causalimpact. The original R package is at https://google.github.io/CausalImpact/.
course_use: Lab: effect of a market launch or campaign in one country; free

title: Matched Markets / Time-Based Regression (TBR) for geo experiments
author_source: Google; GitHub google/matched_markets; Apache-2.0; Python; research code (not an official Google product)
note: Designs geo experiments with a greedy matched-markets search under budget and assignment constraints (TBRMM), and analyses them with time-based regression (Kerman 2017). Includes Colab design and post-analysis notebooks. Small (17 commits) and research-only.
course_use: Optional lab on geo-test design; free

title: Uber Orbit 1.1.5.1 (Bayesian time series, KTR)
author_source: Uber; PyPI orbit-ml/GitHub uber/orbit; v1.1.5.1 released 22 May 2026; Apache-2.0; Python package
note: Bayesian forecasting with exponential smoothing (ETS/LGT/DLT) and Kernel Time-varying Regression (KTR), which Uber has used for time-varying-coefficient MMM (see arXiv 2106.03322). Python 3.12+. Install with pip install orbit-ml. Has about 2.1k stars.
course_use: Advanced option for time-varying effects; free

title: Prophet 1.5.0
author_source: Meta; PyPI/CRAN; v1.5.0 released 5 Oct 2026; MIT; Python and R package
note: Decomposes trend, seasonality and holidays. Robyn uses it for baseline decomposition, and its country holiday support helps multi-country work. Python 3.10+.
course_use: Pre-processing: build trend, season and holiday controls per country; free

title: Nevergrad 1.0.12
author_source: Meta Research; PyPI/GitHub facebookresearch/nevergrad; v1.0.12 released 23 Apr 2025; MIT; Python package
note: Gradient-free optimisation library that Robyn calls through reticulate for multi-objective hyperparameter search. Common install problem in class: point reticulate at a Python 3.8+ environment with nevergrad installed.
course_use: Needed for the Robyn lab; free

title: python-holidays 0.107 (holiday calendars for 250 country codes)
author_source: vacanza community; PyPI holidays; v0.107 released 19 Oct 2026; MIT; Python package
note: Generates national and subdivision (state/region) public holidays for about 250 country codes, with no download step. Use it for holiday dummies in country-level MMM controls with PyMC-Marketing or Meridian. Python 3.10+.
course_use: Lab: build holiday controls for each country in a multi-market panel; free

title: mmm_stan: Python/Stan multiplicative MMM with adstock, ROAS and mROAS
author_source: Sibyl He; GitHub sibylhe/mmm_stan; MIT; Python + Stan repo and notebook
note: Popular tutorial (about 403 stars) that implements the Google Jin et al. Bayesian MMM in Stan. Covers adstock, a multiplicative model, ROAS and marginal ROAS. Includes a 209-week retail dataset. Good for showing what the packages do under the hood.
course_use: Instructor or advanced students: from-scratch Bayesian MMM; free

title: Mamimo: lightweight MMM utilities (scikit-learn style)
author_source: Robert Kübler (Garve); GitHub; licence not stated; Python package
note: Small library with saturation and carryover transformers and time features that fit into scikit-learn pipelines. Useful for a frequentist baseline next to the Bayesian tools. Has about 74 stars and no visible licence or recent releases, so treat it as a teaching illustration only.
course_use: Optional warm-up lab (pipeline with adstock and saturation); free

title: MMM-Guide: Bayesian MMM worked example on a multi-region dataset
author_source: Mark Stent; GitHub markstent/MMM-Guide (fork of mark-allwyn/MMM-Guide); licence not stated; notebooks + FastAPI/Next.js dashboard
note: PyMC/ArviZ notebooks (additive and multiplicative MMM, Shapley decomposition, elasticity-based budget optimisation) using the Figshare multi-region eCommerce MMM dataset (conjura_mmm_data.csv plus data dictionary). Also contains a concept dashboard (MMMpact).
course_use: Template for a student project with real multi-region data; free

title: Robyn dt_simulated_weekly
author_source: Meta Marketing Science; bundled in the Robyn R package (CRAN 3.12.1); MIT; simulated dataset
note: Weekly simulated data loaded with data("dt_simulated_weekly"). Variables: DATE, revenue; spend tv_S, ooh_S, print_S, facebook_S, search_S; exposures facebook_I, search_clicks_P; context competitor_sales_B, events; organic newsletter. The demo models 2016-01-01 to 2018-12-31.
course_use: Standard Robyn lab data; free

title: Robyn dt_prophet_holidays (holiday table for 123 countries)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science; bundled in the Robyn R package; MIT; reference dataset
note: Holiday and event table covering 123 countries, used through prophet_country (for example "DE" or "AT"). You can add school breaks or local events, and you must add countries that are missing. This is the main hook for international adaptation in Robyn.
course_use: Lab: rerun the same model with AT, DE or CH holidays and compare baselines; free

title: Meridian simulated geo datasets (geo_all_channels, geo_media, geo_media_rf, geo_full_funnel_data)
author_source: Google; GitHub google/meridian, meridian/data/simulated_data (csv, xlsx, pkl); Apache-2.0; simulated datasets
note: CSV files: geo_all_channels.csv (media, R&F, organic and non-media treatments), geo_media.csv, geo_media_rf.csv (reach and frequency channels), geo_full_funnel_data.csv and hypothetical_geo_all_channels.csv. They are multi-geo weekly panels with population, controls, KPI and revenue per KPI. Students can treat the geos as countries or regions. The same files are also provided as xlsx and pkl.
course_use: Meridian lab data for geo-hierarchical models; free

title: Meridian simulated national datasets (national_all_channels, national_media, national_media_rf)
author_source: Google; GitHub google/meridian simulated_data/csv; Apache-2.0; simulated datasets
note: National-level (single market) versions of the simulated data, including reach and frequency. Good for contrasting national and geo models: how much precision do geos add?
course_use: Lab comparison of national and geo models; free

title: PyMC-Marketing mmm_multidimensional_example.csv (2-geo panel with true parameters)
author_source: PyMC Labs; GitHub pymc-marketing/data; Apache-2.0; simulated dataset
note: 318 rows: 2 geos x 159 weeks (2022-06-06 to 2025-06-16), channels x1 (always-on) and x2 (tactical), controls event_1 and event_2, target y. The true parameters are in mmm_multidimensional_example_true_parameters.nc, so students can check whether the model recovers them. The folder also has multidimensional_mock_data.csv.
course_use: Lab data for the geo-MMM notebook and parameter-recovery exercise; free

title: PyMC-Marketing example data: mmm_example, mmm_roas_data, media_tvp_data, funnel_data, credibility_* files
author_source: PyMC Labs; GitHub pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/data; Apache-2.0; simulated datasets
note: mmm_example.csv (quickstart MMM), mmm_roas_data.csv (ROAS calibration), media_tvp_data.csv (time-varying effects), funnel_data.csv (funnel mediation), credibility_* files (campaign reach, audience overlap, ground-truth contributions) and fivetran_examples. The folder also holds CLV data (clv_quickstart.csv, cdnow_transactions.csv) and choice data.
course_use: Lab and homework data for every PyMC-Marketing notebook; free

title: Multi-Region Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) Dataset for Several eCommerce Brands (Conjura)
author_source: Conjura; figshare article 25314841; anonymised real-world dataset (licence on the figshare page, not checked)
note: Anonymised multi-region marketing and online purchase data for close to 100 eCommerce brands. Channels: Google, Meta, TikTok. Comes with a data dictionary and is intended for benchmarking CAC and ROAS estimation. Used in the MMM-Guide repo with weekly aggregation. One of the few free real-data, multi-region MMM sets. Check the licence and the regions covered before using it in class.
course_use: Project data for multi-region or international MMM with real spend; free download

title: mmm_stan retail dataset (209 weeks, 13 channels, macro controls)
author_source: Sibyl He; GitHub sibylhe/mmm_stan data.csv; MIT; semi-real anonymised dataset
note: 209 weekly records with sales; impressions (mdip_) and spend (mdsp_) for 13 channels (TV, radio, SEM, email and others); controls for CPI, gas price, store count, markdowns, retail holidays and seasonality. Single market. Useful because it already contains macro controls such as CPI.
course_use: Homework: fit the same data in all three tools; free

title: World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI)
author_source: World Bank; Data Catalog; version 131, updated 9 Oct 2026; CC BY 4.0; statistical database and API
note: Over 1,500 annual indicators for more than 200 countries (1960-2025): GDP per capita (PPP), CPI inflation, population, internet users, mobile subscriptions. Access through the API or the R/Python packages wbstats and wbgapi. Use for country-level covariates and for scaling (population) in geo MMM.
course_use: Country controls for multi-country MMM projects; open licence

title: ITU ICT Statistics (internet use, mobile broadband, by country)
author_source: International Telecommunication Union (ITU-D); statistics portal; time series 2005-2025; Excel download
note: Free Excel series of individuals using the Internet (by sex, age, urban/rural), mobile phone ownership, and fixed and mobile broadband subscriptions and traffic. Useful for explaining cross-country differences in digital channel effectiveness. The page does not state reuse terms.
course_use: Country moderators for comparing digital ROI across markets; free download

title: ECB Data Portal: Exchange Rates (EXR)
author_source: European Central Bank; ECB Data Portal; daily, monthly and annual series; SDMX API; free reuse with source attribution
note: Euro reference exchange rates against about 30 currencies, daily and averaged by period. Needed to convert multi-country media spend and revenue into one currency (EUR) before pooling markets in an MMM. API: https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/ (SDMX REST).
course_use: Data preparation: currency harmonisation for international panels; free

title: Eurostat HICP monthly price index (prc_hicp_midx)
author_source: Eurostat; Eurostat data browser and API; monthly; free reuse with attribution
note: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices by EU/EEA country and COICOP category, monthly. Use it to deflate spend and sales, or as a price or inflation control in European multi-country MMM. Access through the eurostat R package or the Python eurostat package.
course_use: Country controls and deflation for EU market panels; free

title: Eurostat: Internet use and e-commerce by individuals (isoc_ci_ifp_iu, isoc_ec_ib20)
author_source: Eurostat; ICT usage in households and by individuals survey; annual; free reuse with attribution
note: Annual country-level shares of internet users and online shoppers in EU countries. Use them as moderators of digital channel effects across European markets, or to explain why pooled priors differ by country.
course_use: Project: explain country differences in channel ROI; free

title: OECD Data Explorer (CPI, consumer confidence, GDP, PPPs)
author_source: OECD; OECD Data Explorer; SDMX API; monthly, quarterly and annual; free reuse (OECD terms)
note: Monthly consumer confidence (CCI), CPI, unemployment, quarterly GDP and PPP conversion factors for OECD and partner countries. Higher frequency than WDI, so better suited to weekly or monthly MMM controls after interpolation.
course_use: Macro controls for multi-country MMM; free

title: Google Trends (search interest by country and region)
author_source: Google; Google Trends web interface (CSV export); free; index data (0-100)
note: Weekly search interest for brand or category terms by country and subregion. Use it as a demand or brand-interest proxy or a competitive control in MMM. Values are relative indices, and samples can change between downloads.
course_use: Homework: build a brand-search control for each market; free

title: Nager.Date public holiday API
author_source: Nager (open-source project); REST API and GitHub nager/Nager.Date; free; holiday data
note: Free JSON API for public holidays across many countries, with no API key. An alternative to python-holidays and Robyn's dt_prophet_holidays for building holiday dummies in R or Python. The URL currently redirects to nagerholidays.com.
course_use: Data preparation: holiday calendars for each market; free

course_use: Students RSVP free on Meetup; possible venue to present course projects on open-source MMM; on site Vienna.

title: PyCon Austria
author_source: Volunteer, non-profit Python conference; Eisenstadt (FH Burgenland); conference
note: Annual free Python conference in Austria (2025 and 2026 held; next 11-12 April 2027 in Eisenstadt); call for speakers via Sessionize, talks mainly English with German allowed. Good stage for PyMC-Marketing or Meridian talks with an Austrian audience.
course_use: Students attend free; teams could submit a talk on a multi-market MMM project; about one hour from Vienna.

title: Vienna<-R user group
author_source: Vienna R community on Meetup (named with VDSG and Vienna Deep Learning Meetup as the main Vienna data groups); local community
note: Local R community, relevant for Robyn (an R package); talks and networking with Vienna R users from finance and industry. English, German.
course_use: Join via Meetup; suggest an R/Robyn lightning talk by students; on site Vienna.

title: MMA Global (Marketing + Media Alliance)
author_source: Global trade association of marketers; events, think tanks, speaker network; industry community
note: Runs marketing effectiveness and measurement initiatives with brands, agencies and research firms across regions; its speaker profiles (e.g. Kantar analytics leads) are a source of MMM practitioners. English.
course_use: Use speaker lists to find guest speakers; some content needs membership login.

title: MARKETING X and Tag des Marketing (Austrian Marketing Confederation)
author_source: Austrian marketing conferences in Wien; industry events
note: MARKETING X (Novotel Wien Hauptbahnhof, Oct 2025, 60 speakers incl. ÖBB and WPP Media) and the Tag des Marketing of the Austrian Marketing Confederation are the main Austrian marketing practitioner stages; no MMM session found in the 2024/2025 programmes, so measurement is a gap there. German.
course_use: Students attend to network with Austrian marketers and scout DACH guest speakers; German.

title: Geometric adstock (carryover decay)
author_source: Broadbent, S. (1979), J. Market Research Society; tool docs (PyMC-Marketing, Meridian, Robyn)
note: Ad effect decays by constant rate per period. PyMC-Marketing GeometricAdstock(l_max=..., alpha prior; half-life option); Meridian default adstock_decay_spec='geometric' with max_lag; Robyn adstock='geometric' (theta). Pitfall: l_max/max_lag truncation and decay bounds drive ROI; theta ranges differ by medium.
course_use: Lecture 2 (MMM building blocks); spreadsheet exercise computing adstock by hand; free.

title: Weibull adstock (CDF/PDF, delayed peak)
author_source: Robyn docs; Zhou, Lares et al. (Meta)
note: Flexible time-varying decay; PDF variant allows lagged peak. Robyn adstock='weibull_cdf'/'weibull_pdf' (shape, scale); PyMC-Marketing WeibullCDFAdstock/WeibullPDFAdstock (kernel length fix in 1.3.0). Pitfall: needs more iterations, overfits short series.
course_use: Lab: compare geometric vs Weibull fit in Robyn on demo data; free.

title: Delayed / binomial adstock
author_source: Jin et al. (2017) Google; Meridian 1.2.0 changelog
note: Delayed adstock with peak lag (PyMC-Marketing DelayedAdstock); binomial decay (Meridian adstock_decay_spec='binomial', PyMC-Marketing BinomialAdstock). Pitfall: peak lag weakly identified without strong flighting variation.
course_use: Lecture slot on TV vs digital carryover; free.

title: Hill saturation (diminishing returns)
author_source: Jin, Wang, Sun, Chan & Koehler (2017), Google Research
note: S-shaped response with half-saturation (ec/gamma) and slope/alpha. Meridian Hill(ec, slope), hill_before_adstock flag; Robyn Hill (alpha, gamma); PyMC-Marketing HillSaturation/HillSaturationSigmoid. Pitfall: saturation is poorly identified without spend variation; geo data helps.
course_use: Lecture 2; interactive response-curve plotting exercise; free.

title: Logistic / Michaelis-Menten / tanh saturation
author_source: PyMC-Marketing docs (PyMC Labs)
note: Alternative concave curves: LogisticSaturation (default in many PyMC-Marketing examples), MichaelisMentenSaturation, TanhSaturation. Pitfall: different curves yield different marginal ROI at the same fit; compare with LOO.
course_use: Advanced lab: swap saturation classes, compare mROAS; free.

title: Bayesian MMM with carryover and shape effects
author_source: Jin, Y., Wang, Y., Sun, Y., Chan, D., Koehler, J. (2017), Google Inc. technical report
note: Foundational Bayesian MMM paper (priors, ROAS/mROAS from posterior); basis for LightweightMMM and Meridian. Pitfall: priors dominate in small samples (paper's own finding).
course_use: Core reading week 1-2; free PDF.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian partial pooling across geos/countries
author_source: Sun, Y., Wang, Y., Jin, Y., Chan, D., Koehler, J. (2017), 'Geo-level Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Modeling', Google
note: Geo coefficients drawn around a national mean; tighter intervals than national models. Meridian built-in (eta_m, xi_c; media_effects_dist); PyMC-Marketing via dims=('geo',) and Prior(..., dims=('channel','geo'), centered=False). Robyn: not supported. Pitfall: pooling countries with different KPI definitions or currencies.
course_use: Lecture on international MMM; lab: DACH panel with AT as small geo; free.

title: Population scaling / per-capita modelling
author_source: Meridian input-data docs (Google)
note: Meridian requires geo population and scales KPI and media per capita; control_population_scaling_id for controls; 2.1.0 ModelSpec population scaling. PyMC-Marketing: scaling argument (per-geo max-abs). Pitfall: per-capita ignores purchasing power differences.
course_use: Exercise: compute per-capita spend for EU countries; free.

title: ROI / mROI prior parameterisation
author_source: Wurm, M., Price, B., Liu, Y. (2024), 'Media Mix Model Calibration With Bayesian Priors', Google Research
note: Reparameterise model so ROI is a parameter; set LogNormal priors from experiments/benchmarks. Meridian media_prior_type='roi'|'mroi'|'contribution'|'coefficient', roi_m/roi_rf, lognormal_dist_from_range; PyMC-Marketing add_cost_per_target_calibration. Pitfall: too-tight priors become the answer; check prior-posterior shift.
course_use: Lecture on priors; elicitation exercise with country managers' beliefs; free.

title: Lift-test / experiment calibration
author_source: PyMC-Marketing lift-test notebook; Robyn calibration docs; Meridian CalibrationBuilder
note: PyMC-Marketing add_lift_test_measurements (channel, x, delta_x, delta_y, sigma) as observations of saturation curve; Robyn calibration_input + MAPE.LIFT objective; Meridian experiments -> ROI priors (CalibrationBuilder, GeoX). Pitfall: estimand mismatch (experiment counterfactual vs MMM zero-spend baseline), spend mismatch (Robyn: within 10%).
course_use: Lab: calibrate model with a synthetic lift test; free.

title: Ridge regression + Nevergrad multi-objective hyperparameter search
author_source: Runge, J., Skokan, I., Zhou, G., Pauwels, K. (2024), arXiv:2403.14674
note: Robyn: glmnet ridge for coefficients; Nevergrad TwoPointsDE searches adstock/saturation/lambda/train_size; robyn_run(iterations, trials). Pitfall: many equally good models; results vary by seed and analyst choice.
course_use: Lecture on frequentist vs Bayesian MMM; Robyn demo lab; free.

title: DECOMP.RSSD and Pareto-front model selection
author_source: Robyn features docs (Meta)
note: Decomposition root-sum-squared distance between spend shares and effect shares; minimised jointly with NRMSE (and MAPE.LIFT); Pareto front then k-means clusters; objective_weights. Pitfall: penalises true outliers (very efficient small channels) — a business prior, not a statistical truth.
course_use: Discussion: is RSSD a sensible assumption in a new market?; free.

title: Prophet time-series decomposition
author_source: Taylor, S. J., Letham, B. (2018), 'Forecasting at Scale', The American Statistician 72(1)
note: Robyn prophet_vars (trend, season, monthly, weekday, holiday), prophet_country with bundled holidays (123 countries). Pitfall: prophet trend can absorb media effects; two-stage approach ignores uncertainty.
course_use: Lab: inspect Robyn decomposition for AT vs DE holidays; paper paid, preprint free (PeerJ).

title: Fourier seasonality
author_source: Harvey (1990); PyMC-Marketing fourier module
note: PyMC-Marketing yearly_seasonality=n Fourier modes (gamma_fourier priors, per-geo dims). Pitfall: too many modes overfit; hemisphere differences across countries.
course_use: Short lecture block; free docs.

title: Time-varying intercept via knots (Meridian AKS)
author_source: Meridian docs: setting knots
note: Baseline interpolated between knots (knots argument); automatic knot selection (enable_aks, AIC since 1.2.1). Pitfall: one knot per period saturates national models.
course_use: Lab: vary knots and observe ROI shifts; free.

title: Gaussian-process (HSGP) time-varying coefficients
author_source: Riutort-Mayol, G., et al. (2023), 'Practical Hilbert space approximate Bayesian Gaussian processes', Statistics and Computing 33
note: PyMC-Marketing time_varying_intercept / time_varying_media with HSGP config; composable HSGP terms (1.3.0). Not in Meridian (media) or Robyn. Pitfall: confounds with trend; needs priors on lengthscale.
course_use: Advanced seminar; open access paper.

title: Reach & frequency modelling
author_source: Zhang, Y., Wurm, M., Liu, Y., et al. (2023), 'Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Model Incorporating Reach and Frequency Data', Google
note: Effect = reach x Hill(frequency), adstocked; Meridian native R&F inputs and optimal_freq(); Robyn curve calibrator (beta). Pitfall: R&F availability differs by country/platform.
course_use: Lecture on frequency planning for YouTube/Meta campaigns; free.

title: Geo experiments / synthetic control (GeoLift)
author_source: Meta Open Source, GeoLift (R package); Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2010) JASA synthetic control
note: Market selection, power analysis and inference for geo tests via synthetic control (augsynth); output feeds Robyn calibration_input. Pitfall: few comparable regions in small countries.
course_use: Lab: design a GeoLift test across Austrian regions; free.

title: Matched markets / trimmed match geo experiments (GeoX)
author_source: Chen, A., Au, T. C. (2022), 'Robust causal inference for incremental return on ad spend with randomized paired geo experiments', Annals of Applied Statistics 16(1)
note: Google's trimmed match underpins GeoX; Meridian 2.0 imports GeoX results as priors (with_meridian_geox_experiment_result, [geox] extra). Pitfall: requires many geos; often infeasible for single small countries.
course_use: Lecture on incrementality testing; paper paid (arXiv preprint free).

title: Budget optimisation with response curves
author_source: Tool docs: Meridian BudgetOptimizer, PyMC-Marketing BudgetOptimizer, Robyn robyn_allocator
note: Equalise marginal ROI under constraints. PyMC-Marketing SLSQP with budget_bounds per channel x geo; Meridian optimize(fixed_budget, target_roi/target_mroi, spend_constraint_lower/upper); Robyn max_response / target_efficiency with channel_constr_low/up. Pitfall: extrapolating beyond observed spend ranges; ignoring uncertainty.
course_use: Case exercise: allocate a DACH budget; free.

title: Posterior predictive checks & MCMC diagnostics
author_source: Gelman, A., et al. (2013), Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., CRC; ArviZ
note: sample_posterior_predictive (PyMC-Marketing), R-hat/PPP check/ModelReviewer (Meridian). Not applicable to Robyn. Pitfall: good in-sample fit does not imply causal validity.
course_use: Lab checkpoint after every fit; BDA free PDF on author site.

title: Causal DAG thinking in MMM
author_source: Pearl (2009) Causality; PyMC-Marketing dag / treatment_nodes / outcome_node
note: Use DAG to choose controls (confounders vs mediators); PyMC-Marketing supports DAG-based identification and pm.do interventions; Meridian distinguishes controls vs treatments. Pitfall: controlling for mediators (e.g. branded search) removes media effect.
course_use: Workshop: draw DAG for a multi-country FMCG brand; free docs.

title: Out-of-sample / time-series validation
author_source: Robyn ts_validation; Meridian holdout_id
note: Robyn train/val/test split with NRMSE on test; Meridian holdout_id / ModelSpec holdouts; PyMC-Marketing out-of-sample prediction. Pitfall: fit-based validation does not validate causal ROI; combine with experiments.
course_use: Lab: hold out last 13 weeks per country; free.

title: Model refresh
author_source: Robyn robyn_refresh docs/demo
note: robyn_refresh() for incremental updates (<=50% new data); Bayesian tools refit with previous posterior as prior (manual). Pitfall: refresh drift, inconsistent specs across countries.
course_use: Discussion of governance for multi-market MMM programmes; free.

title: Currency / PPP normalisation for multi-country spend
author_source: OECD/Eurostat PPP statistics; World Bank ICP
note: Convert local spend/revenue to a common currency (fixed or period-average FX) and optionally PPP before pooling countries; none of the three tools does this automatically (Meridian only labels currency_code). Pitfall: FX swings create artificial spend variation; PPP vs market FX change efficiency rankings.
course_use: Exercise: convert CEE spend to EUR and PPP, rerun pooled model; free data.

title: Lightweight / packaging perspective on MMM adoption
author_source: Runge, Skokan, Zhou, Pauwels (2024) arXiv; Chan & Perry (2017) 'Challenges and Opportunities in Media Mix Modeling', Google
note: Critical overview of MMM limitations (data, selection bias, endogeneity). Pitfall: treating tool output as truth.
course_use: Opening lecture reading; free.

title: 12 Best Practices for a Successful Marketing Mix Modeling Investment
author_source: Brian Lange, Ipsos MMA (Marketing Management Analytics), 22 Oct 2024
note: Vendor list running from clear objectives through cadence, external factors, granular data, continuous validation and scenario use. Qualitative, no numbers. Do not confuse this MMA, a modelling firm owned by Ipsos, with MMA Global, the trade association. Search found no MMA Global MMM standard.
course_use: Short comparison reading against the IAB guide. Free.

title: Bayesian MMM across geographies (hierarchical geo guide)
author_source: MetricGate documentation, 27 May 2026 (vendor)
note: Compact explanation of partial pooling with explicit, though unsourced, rules: a between-geo spread to population mean ratio (tau over mu) above 0.3 signals strong heterogeneity; at least 5 geos with 10 or more observations each for a usable population estimate. Single-channel, Gaussian, exchangeable geos. Teach the thresholds as heuristics to be tested, not findings.
course_use: Short reading before the hierarchical lab; test the 0.3 rule by simulation. Free.

title: Bayesian Workflow (mmm-framework documentation)
author_source: mmm-framework project documentation, built on PyMC (no named author on the page)
note: Applied version of the Gelman workflow for MMM. Prior predictive draws should be broader than observed data and put no mass on negative sales; refit under alternative priors; backtest coverage near nominal 0.9. Sampler gates: R-hat below 1.01, bulk and tail ESS above 400, zero divergences, Pareto k above 0.7 flags influential points; accept a model expansion only if ELPD improves by more than one standard error. Independent project, not PyMC Labs. No official PyMC Labs best-practice guide was found, this is the nearest equivalent.
course_use: Technical reference for the priors and diagnostics lab. Free.

title: Can I optimize budget by geo? Meridian GitHub Discussion #618
author_source: google/meridian maintainers and users, April 2025 to February 2026
note: Essential limitation for international teaching. Maintainers state the optimizer does not automatically shift a total budget between geos and assumes historical flighting. Workaround: loop over geos with selected_geos, then split the total manually. Per-geo outcomes are available through aggregate_geos=False. Check against the current release before teaching, last maintainer reply seen is February 2026.
course_use: Lab: write the manual two-stage country allocation. Free.

title: Google Meridian Data Collection Playbook (March 2026)
author_source: NIQ Media (Nielsen Consumer LLC), vendor and Meridian partner
note: 25-page project-management guide, rare in being about the unglamorous work. Rule of thumb of at least 15 observations per variable, so a 104-week national model holds about 7 variables including knots; keep media variables below 20. Base timeline for a single model: 4 weeks collection, 3 review, 5 modelling, 2 presentation. Includes kick-off agenda and data templates. Vendor document ending with a sales offer; US and Canada examples, no multi-country section.
course_use: Project planning template for student teams; multiply the timeline by number of markets. Free PDF.

title: How often should you retrain your Marketing Mix Model?
author_source: Lauri Potka, Sellforte, 28 Aug 2026 (vendor)
note: Vendor position at the far end of the debate: retrain nightly for digital media when checks pass. Useful distinctions: a data refresh is not a retrain, convergence does not prove stability, offline inputs arriving weekly or monthly cap the learning rate, and new variables usually need a rebuild. Sellforte sells nightly retraining, so set it against the IAB guide's warning that retraining too often amplifies noise.
course_use: Paired reading for a refresh-cadence debate. Free.

title: How should we weight multiple incrementality tests when calibrating an MMM?
author_source: Lauri Potka, Sellforte, 18 Aug 2026 (vendor)
note: Four-factor scoring of each test: relevance, recency (explicit decay reviewed by channel and market), statistical confidence, spend. Do not average test iROAS equally; exclude invalid tests but keep them in the library. Gives no numeric weights or formula, so students must build and defend their own. Complements the same author's cross-country transfer article already in the guide.
course_use: Exercise: score five fictional country tests and derive a prior. Free.

title: IAB draft Cross-Channel Measurement Decision Guide (public comment, Oct 2026), coverage
author_source: PPC Land reporting on IAB Project Eidos
note: Released 20 Oct 2026, comments to 4 Nov 2026, final date unannounced. Does not pick a winner when MMM, incrementality and attribution disagree; prescribes a seven-step sequence from business outcome through decision, measurement question, approach, evidence, interpretation to action. Interpretive framework, not a specification. Draft status: check for the final version before the course starts.
course_use: Background for a triangulation case discussion. Free article.

title: MMM accuracy vs confidence
author_source: Analytic Partners, 22 Jul 2026 (vendor)
note: Argues statistical fit shows a model is well built, not that forward decisions hold; judge by forecasts against outcomes. Cites a survey: 82% of MMM users get results at least quarterly and only 6.1% weekly; sample and method not given here. Vendor argument that outside benchmarks are needed, which also sells its product.
course_use: Background; survey figures for the cadence discussion, with caveat. Free.

title: Market Mix Modelling Landscape Report 2025 (updated December 2025)
author_source: IAB Australia Ad Effectiveness Council
note: 141-page original (page count from Mumbrella, 18 Sept 2025) profiling twelve vendors including Meta Robyn, Google Meridian, Recast, Analytic Partners, Mutinex, Kantar; December 2025 update adds Adobe, Monks and Mortar AI. Each profile covers method, validation, data requirements, refresh cadence. Vendor self-descriptions, so read comparatively rather than as evidence. Australian market.
course_use: Reference for a vendor comparison seminar; career session on who employs MMM analysts. Free PDF.

title: Market Mix Modelling: Marketers Checklist (2025)
author_source: IAB Australia Ad Effectiveness Council
note: Two-page tick-box form in eight stages: strategic foundations, measurement framework, data readiness, stakeholder alignment, vendor and model selection, compare and test models, implementation and validation, actionability. Rules are qualitative: compare out-of-sample margin of error across candidate models, calibrate with lift tests, monitor for model drift after deployment, name a project champion. Short enough to hand out unchanged.
course_use: In-class audit tool: student teams score a published MMM case against it. Free PDF.

title: Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM): Resources (ANA package)
author_source: Association of National Advertisers
note: Index of ANA material dated to Jan 2026: Media Mix Modeling cheat sheet, checklist and Quick Win package, plus items from 2024. Members only, contents not seen, so no recommendation can be reported. Listed so the course can follow up if access exists.
course_use: Optional; check whether WU or a guest speaker's employer has ANA membership. Members only.

title: Marketing mix modeling best practices: Understanding why regional data delivers more accurate results than national data
author_source: Nielsen (Japan study, 2022)
note: 11 pages. 19 Nielsen Japanese MMMs re-run at both levels: regional average R-squared 96% and MAPE 4% versus national 86% and 7%; 66% of variables showed lift regionally versus 16% nationally. Footnote study: leaving out non-media drivers inflated ROI by 68%. Vendor study, FMCG and e-commerce only, and in-sample fit favours more data points, so it does not prove better causal estimates. URL is a Nielsen development host.
course_use: Critique exercise: what does higher R-squared actually show? Free PDF.

title: Meridian Self-starter Guide for CMOs (July 2025)
author_source: Google; Olesya Moosman, Lauren Sheridan, Aleksandra Algina (Google MMM leads, UK and Northern Europe)
note: 14-page non-technical roadmap for in-house builds. Recommends 2 to 3 years of data (4 to 5 for long purchase cycles or long-term effects), C-level sponsor, team mixing data science, econometrics, BI and marketing. Says R-squared above 0.80 is pretty good and 0.90 or above is achievable. Useful output-reading section on baseline, contribution, ROI versus marginal ROI. Notes mature markets with high awareness should show higher baselines than growth markets, a usable cross-country sanity check. Compare its R-squared rule with Meridian's own docs, which warn against treating fit as the main criterion.
course_use: Reading for managers; basis for an interpret-the-output session. Free PDF.

title: Meridian: Amount of data needed
author_source: Google for Developers, Meridian documentation
note: Works through data points per parameter. National example: 104 weeks with 26 parameters gives about 4 per parameter, called too low; 156 weeks with 10 parameters gives about 15, still only directional. Geo example: 105 geos over 3 years gives 16,380 points, about 8 per parameter under no pooling and about 74 under perfect pooling. Sets no fixed minimum. For sparse geos suggests combining channels or a tighter prior such as HalfNormal(0.1) on eta_m and xi_c. Does not mention countries.
course_use: Lab: compute the ratio for a 6-country, 104-week panel and decide what to cut. Free.

title: Meridian: Collect and organize your data
author_source: Google for Developers, Meridian documentation
note: States geo-level weekly data as best practice, at least 2 years for geo models and 3 for national. Zero-fill missing media but not KPI or controls. Metrics must be summable across geo and time, so convert CTR to clicks. Controls should be real confounders, found by asking planners what shaped decisions. Holiday dummies generally unnecessary because seasonality is handled, which needs discussion when countries have different calendars. No guidance on currency or multi-country data, a gap worth naming in class.
course_use: Reading before the data-preparation lab. Free.

title: Meridian: General product FAQs (pooling and calibration entries)
author_source: Google for Developers, Meridian documentation
note: Key for multi-country models: media and control coefficients are partially pooled, but time effects, adstock and diminishing-returns parameters are assumed common across geos, so a country panel forces shared carryover and saturation. Geo modelling assumes KPI and media units mean essentially the same across geos. For calibration, use a spend-weighted average ROI across experiments and weight by standard error. Nothing on currency or on comparing countries.
course_use: Short reading, then debate whether the shared-saturation assumption holds between Germany and Poland. Free.

title: Meridian: Model fit and validation
author_source: Google for Developers, Meridian documentation
note: Argues the goal is causal inference, not prediction error. Holdout R-squared, MAPE and wMAPE are only a preliminary overparameterisation check, and some overfitting is acceptable if ROI stays unbiased. Warning signs: low or negative baseline, one channel dominating. Gives no numeric cutoffs. Pairs well with the CMO guide, which offers an R-squared rule.
course_use: Reading for the validation session. Free.

title: Meridian: Model health score
author_source: Google for Developers, Meridian documentation
note: Composite 0 to 100 score. Non-converged models score zero. Bayesian PPP passes at 0.05 or higher; negative baseline passes when probability is below 0.2 and fails above 0.8; R-squared is mapped on a sigmoid steepest between 0.3 and 0.7. Overall 90 or higher suggests the model can support decisions, 70 or lower suggests systematic error. Related health-check page uses max R-hat below 1.2 as the convergence pass. Compare with the stricter R-hat 1.01 in the mmm-framework workflow guide.
course_use: Lab acceptance gate for student models. Free.

title: Models as Masters? Marketing Mix Modeling and AI-Driven Media Decision Making (July 2026)
author_source: Chris Williams and Jon Watts, CIMM (Coalition for Innovative Media Measurement; copyright ARF Innovation Studio)
note: 53-page industry paper, the closest thing found to ARF-linked guidance. Six practical steps: MMM-ready media data specification, standard model factsheet (data sources, priors, adstock, excluded variables, validation, refresh cadence, conflicts of interest), experimentation and validation playbook, shared evidence library, contractual toolkit, engagement with agentic protocol developers. Argues influence shifts from outputs to inputs such as priors. TV and video focus, US-centred. Contributors include Google, Meta, Ebiquity and Mutinex.
course_use: Reading on governance and platform power; students draft a model factsheet. Free PDF.

title: Modernizing MMM: Best Practices for Marketers (December 2025)
author_source: IAB (US), Measurement, Addressability and Data Center, with MMM providers and practitioners
note: 30-page vendor-neutral guide in six areas, about ten numbered practices each with why and caveat. Actual rules: minimum 2 years of weekly history (3 to 4 preferred) or 1 to 2 years daily; record spend by run date and keep a log of currency conversions; weekly input refresh with full retrain monthly or quarterly; require at least two supporting signals for material decisions; only use experiments that match KPI, geography and window; five to 10% variance as an example threshold between auto-action and review; 24 to 48 hour SLAs. Landing page offers a free RFI question template. US framing (DMA, ZIP), no country-level section.
course_use: Core reading and basis for a checklist exercise; RFI template for a vendor-selection assignment. Free PDF.

title: The MMM handbook: A guide for developing impactful marketing mix models
author_source: Google, Think with Google (PDF created Feb 2023)
note: 13-page interactive checklist in seven sections from business questions to partner deliverables. Recommends avoiding cost as a media input because bidding makes it misleading, using clicks, impressions or views instead; stacking data by geography or product to raise the variable limit; distinguishing time periods so ROI can change. Interesting tension for class: this 2023 handbook favours campaign-level inputs while current Meridian guidance says to stay at channel level. Google-authored, so read channel advice critically.
course_use: Short reading plus discussion of how platform guidance changed between 2023 and 2026. Free PDF.

title: The Paid Media Effectiveness Handbook (WFA and Ebiquity, July 2026), press summary
author_source: World Federation of Advertisers with Ebiquity
note: Multinational-advertiser evidence: survey of 71 senior leaders in 10 sectors plus 25 interviews, advertisers responsible for USD 40bn annual spend. Eight in 10 run MMM, only 15% say effectiveness evidence is the primary driver of budgets, 13% are strong on speed from data to insight, 46% sit at the lowest data-integration maturity, over 60% rate walled gardens a severe or critical challenge. The handbook itself is for WFA members; this page gives findings only, no MMM method detail. Self-selected sample.
course_use: Motivating slide for the governance session; check whether WU holds WFA access. Summary free, handbook members only.

title: These 5 factors will tell you when to refresh your marketing mix model
author_source: Tim Fisher, SVP Measurement and Head of EMEA, Monks (undated, copyright 2026)
note: Cadence rule set: monthly for high-quality data and fast markets with automated pipelines; quarterly as default; biannual for stable, data-limited markets; rebuild after structural change such as a launch, pricing shift or new channel. Five factors: data quality, business speed, analytical capability, decision cadence, stability versus responsiveness. Agency view, but its logic supports different cadences per market within one programme.
course_use: Reading; assign a cadence to three contrasting markets. Free.

title: A PyMC-Marketing Case Study: Campaign Dynamics, Influencer Effectiveness, and Time-Slice CV (Nürnberger, Part III)
author_source: Teemu Säilynoja, Niall Oulton, Timothy McWilliams, PyMC Labs (updated 2 Jun 2026)
note: Third part of the German insurer case; the earlier guide has only the first post. Covers campaign-segment multipliers, an influencer reach and quality split, and cross-validation when channels launch mid-series. About 18 minutes. No software version stated; published before PyMC-Marketing 1.0, so treat any API detail as pre-1.0. No geo content. The 27 percent CPL reduction is a vendor claim.
course_use: German client example for an advanced session. Free.

title: Business Punk interview with Markus Repetschnig on marketing analytics (German)
author_source: André Patrzek, Business Punk (no date shown; images from March 2026)
note: German founder view of MMM as one of several measurement lenses for omnichannel brands next to server-side tracking and experiments. Thin on method. The statement that Admetrics' MMM is industry-leading is a vendor claim.
course_use: Optional German practitioner voice; career or start-up angle. Free.

title: Globales MMM, lokale Realität (German)
author_source: Inna Ivanova-Genova, Kantar (5 Nov 2026)
note: German-language piece on governance of international MMM programmes with three models: central decisions, global steering with local co-responsibility, local decisions within a shared framework. No data, cases or named countries. The claim that the hybrid is often the best balance is vendor opinion.

author_source: Brice de Matharel and Ivan Yuen, fifty-five (17 May 2024)
