title: Why Marketing Mix Models Fail
author_source: Rocco De Rosa and Teemu Säilynoja, PyMC Labs (updated 21 Oct 2026)
note: Four failure modes on an invented USD 200M brand: priors from spend share reproduce the existing plan, convergence is not validation, baselines absorb media effects (one control halved media contribution), fit is not attribution. About 18 minutes. No software version named and no multi-country analysis. Vendor-written.
course_use: Reading before model critique; suits non-technical students. Free.

title: Why Your Marketing Mix Model Should See the Funnel
author_source: Juan Orduz, PyMC Labs (updated 3 Sep 2026)
note: Non-technical companion to the funnel notebooks. On synthetic data with three regions, the funnel model had under 9 percent average ROAS error against 19 to 33 percent for conventional specifications, and it reversed one budget move (TV in the south). Author's caveats: synthetic data, in-sample budget results, notebook code rather than a shipped feature. About 18 minutes. Vendor-written.
course_use: Reading on mediation and search credit. Free.

author_source: Leeflang, Wieringa, Bijmolt, Pauwels (eds.), Springer 2017

title: Austrian digital tax data on platform ad bookings (Der Standard)
author_source: Der Standard, on Finance Ministry revenue from digital tax and advertising levy; article about July 2026

title: BIS effective exchange rate indices
author_source: Bank for International Settlements; nominal and real, base 2020 = 100; viewed 9 Nov 2026

course_use: Control variable in student models. Free.

title: Ebiquity 2026 Media Budgets Report
author_source: Ebiquity; survey covering 17 markets and over 500 respondents; German page available
note: Advertiser intentions by channel: digital video and connected TV lead budget increases. Survey intentions, not prices or spend. Ebiquity's China view of modest media inflation appears in separate press.

title: Eurostat purchasing power parities and price level indices (prc_ppp_ind)
author_source: Eurostat; dataset confirmed through Eurostat API, 9 Nov 2026; browser view is script-rendered

title: Facebook Ads CPM by country (Lebesgue benchmark)
author_source: Lebesgue; 27 Jul 2026; vendor benchmark with undisclosed sample and method

course_use: Exercise on CPM differences across markets. Free.

title: Focus Werbebilanz via LEADERSNET, January to July 2026 (Austria)
author_source: LEADERSNET, reporting Focus data; 3 Sep 2026

course_use: Local market data for Austrian cases. Free.

title: Frankfurter exchange rate API
author_source: Frankfurter open-source project; no API key; rates from central banks, viewed 9 Nov 2026
note: Daily rates for 219 currencies with history to 1948 from 108 central banks and official sources (project statement), easy to call from a notebook. Blended rates are the project's own calculation, so cite the source provider for research use.
course_use: Lab: build a weekly FX table. Free.

title: IAB Europe AdEx Benchmark 2025 (PDF copy)
author_source: IAB Europe; report on 2025 data, published July 2026; 56 pages; hosted by ADC Group, not by IAB Europe

Figures are charts, so transcribe them. Good for market prioritisation and to size walled-garden categories.
course_use: Project data for market selection; reading for regional differences. Free.

title: IMF Data portal
author_source: International Monetary Fund; API and Excel add-in; terms on the portal's copyright page; viewed 9 Nov 2026
note: Exchange rates and macro controls for countries outside ECB and OECD coverage, which matters for Asia, Africa and Latin America. The home page confirms an API and a data brief on real effective exchange rates; locate the specific dataset through search.
course_use: Project data for emerging-market controls. Free.

author_source: World Bank; results released May 2024; extrapolated GDP PPPs for 2022 and 2023; viewed 9 Nov 2026

author_source: Blake, Nosko, Tadelis (2015), Econometrica

author_source: Puttaparthi Tirumala (2026), Journal of Open Source Software

author_source: Lefrere, Warberg, Cheyre, Marotta, Acquisti (Management Science, 2026 per Crossref)

author_source: Wong, Hughes et al., arXiv 2608.10229 (2026)

title: Examining the relationship of country-level digital ad spend and cross-border e-commerce buyers under cultural and political globalization
author_source: Lee, Yalcinkaya, Griffith (2024), International Marketing Review

title: External Validity and Meta-Analysis
author_source: Slough, Tyson (2022), American Journal of Political Science

title: External Validity: From Do-Calculus to Transportability Across Populations
author_source: Pearl, Bareinboim (2014), Statistical Science

title: Generalizations about Advertising Effectiveness in Markets
author_source: Tellis (2009), Journal of Advertising Research

author_source: Wu, Gu, Deng, Zhu, Chen, arXiv 2606.30992 (submitted June 2026; Airbnb authors)

title: How Important Are Brands? A Cross-Category, Cross-Country Study
author_source: Fischer, Völckner, Sattler (2010), Journal of Marketing Research

title: How Many Countries for Multilevel Modeling? A Comparison of Frequentist and Bayesian Approaches
author_source: Stegmueller (2013), American Journal of Political Science

title: How Well Does Advertising Work? Generalizations from Meta-Analysis of Brand Advertising Elasticities
author_source: Sethuraman, Tellis, Briesch (2011), Journal of Marketing Research
note: 751 short-term and 402 long-term elasticities from 56 studies, 1960 to 2008. Mean short-term 0.12, long-term 0.24, declining over time; higher for durables and early life-cycle stages. title: How to generalize from a hierarchical model?
author_source: Pachali, Kurz, Otter (2020), Quantitative Marketing and Economics

title: Marketing Budget Allocation Across Countries: The Role of International Business Cycles
author_source: Peers, van Heerde, Dekimpe (2017), Marketing Science

title: Marketing mix and brand sales in global markets: Examining the contingent role of country-market characteristics
author_source: Bahadir, Bharadwaj, Srivastava (2015), Journal of International Business Studies

Distribution has the largest effect in emerging and price in developed countries; advertising and innovation effects are larger in emerging markets. The closest academic precursor to a country-pooled MMM with moderators.

title: Measuring Heterogeneity in TV Advertising Elasticities: Evidence from 135 Retail and Restaurant Brands
author_source: Knight, Hsieh, Bart (2026), Journal of Marketing Research
note: Significant heterogeneity by market characteristics for over 93% of 135 US brands. Firms tend to spend where revenue is already high rather than where incremental revenue is highest, overinvesting in dense high-income markets. author_source: Kim (2020), Journal of International Marketing

author_source: Frey, Presidente (2024), Economic Inquiry

title: Reducing Biases in Advertising Effectiveness Research: New Meta-Analytic Evidence
author_source: Korkames, Stanley, Stremersch (2022), SSRN working paper

After correcting for misspecification, aggregation, publication and selection bias the authors report a mean short-term elasticity of .0008 and long-term .03, more than sixfold below earlier meta-analyses. Strong counterpoint to Sethuraman et al.: what happens to a prior if the literature is biased upward? Working paper, not peer reviewed in this version.

title: Site Selection Bias in Program Evaluation
author_source: Allcott (2015), Quarterly Journal of Economics

author_source: Aravindakshan, Peters, Naik (2012), Journal of Marketing Research

author_source: Shapiro, Hitsch, Tuchman (2021), Econometrica

author_source: Dew, Padilla, Shchetkina (2024), arXiv 2408.07678

author_source: Röver (2021), bayesmeta R package, Journal of Statistical Software

title: Budget allocation with minimum-presence thresholds per market
author_source: Abedi (2017), Journal of the Operational Research Society

note: Strongest cross-country teaching point found. Allegro built Meridian models in-house after finding other tools opaque. Short-form video was strong in Poland but much weaker in the Czech model, so the firm stopped copying its Polish strategy and asked whether audience taste or its own creative was the cause. Also found underinvestment in upper funnel. Vendor-written, no ROI or lift figures in the excerpts. Read only through search excerpts because the page sits behind a Google consent redirect from Austria; open it in a browser before citing.
course_use: Case discussion: local response or local execution? How would you test it? Free.

title: Ferrero: portfolio MMM in Italy, Germany, UK and US (Wharton Analytics Accelerator, Fall 2019)
author_source: Wharton AI and Analytics Accelerator, one-page summary
note: Student team model for a named multinational across four markets. Brand halo varied in all four markets and for every brand and product combination, yet Ferrero's global BI head reported enough commonality to run models centrally. Team recommended A/B tests outside holiday season to establish causality. One page, no ROI figures or method detail, software not stated, and it is pre-Meridian.
course_use: Discussion prompt and model for a student-company project format. Free PDF.

title: Haleon: scaling MMM across 120+ brand-market combinations
author_source: Ekimetrics article on a talk by John O'Connor (Haleon) and Olivier Kuziner, Campaign 360 APAC, May 2026; published 16 Jul 2026
note: Best documented rollout found. Timeline: 2 pilot markets 2020, 12 brand-market combinations 2021, 27 to 43 in 2022, over 120 by 2025. Common backbone of data, method and KPIs with room for local adaptation; co-funding from 2022; internal capacity from 2023; self-service dashboards 2025. Vendor claim: over GBP 100 million cumulative value identified since 2021. Markets not named, and not open source as far as stated.
course_use: Lead example for the governance session; guest talk lead. Free.

title: HelloFresh: Bayesian media mix modelling with PyMC, now run in-house
author_source: PyMC Labs case study (undated, copyright 2026; vendor claim)
note: In-house PyMC model rebuilt by PyMC Labs: adstock, reach saturation, log outcome, Student-T likelihood for outlier weeks. Vendor claims prediction variance down 60% and fit time from about 20 to about 2 minutes. HelloFresh operates in many countries, but the page states no markets and no business result, so the international angle has to be asked of a speaker. Technical reparameterisation details useful for advanced students.
course_use: Lab background on model engineering. Free.

title: Hierarchical geo-level Meridian MMM for a multi-retailer enterprise
author_source: Ksolves case study (vendor claim; client unnamed)
note: Up to about 40 geos in an AWS pipeline, budget constraints of plus or minus 30% per channel. Teaching value is in the numbers: pooled R-squared about 0.86 while per-geo R-squared ran about 0.25 to 0.69, used to decide which markets can support local optimisation. Incremental ROI about 1.1 against raw revenue-to-spend of about 6.8x. Client and geography unnamed, and the page is internally inconsistent on some figures.
course_use: Lab discussion: pooled fit can hide weak local fit. Free.

title: MMM case studies: Nexon (Korea) and Suntory Wellness (Japan)
author_source: Google, Think with Google APAC (vendor claim), with Analytic Edge and Mutinex
note: Korea and Japan examples. Nexon study with Analytic Edge found a 20% increase in Google's incremental media contribution to its core KPI. Suntory Wellness, with Mutinex, found YouTube had the longest adstock of its digital media and said it planned to adopt Meridian. So these are partner models rather than confirmed open-source builds. Every result published favours the publisher's channels. Excerpts only, consent redirect.
course_use: Example of channel-owner reporting bias; Asian-market reference. Free.

title: Marketing mix modelling mindset shifts (Dream11, Mondelez, Honasa, India)
author_source: Google, Think with Google India (vendor-written)
note: Indian advertisers using regular MMM, including the local arm of a multinational. Excerpts describe Dream11 rebalancing media spend. No method or result detail seen and no evidence of open-source tools. Consent redirect, excerpts only; verify before use.
course_use: Minor example for emerging-market adoption. Free.

title: Marketing mix modelling with Meridian: APAC meta-analysis of partner projects
author_source: Google, Think with Google APAC (vendor claim)

Partner-delivered and commissioned by the tool's owner. Could not open the page (consent redirect), read through excerpts only.
course_use: Critical reading on who reports MMM results. Free.

title: Meblobranie.pl: three-month Meridian build at a Polish furniture retailer
author_source: Google, Think with Google (vendor-written)

title: TikTok and Yotta: meta-analysis of 11 Polish MMM projects, 2022 to 2025
author_source: TikTok business blog, analysis by Yotta (Publicis Groupe) (vendor claim, commissioned by TikTok; copyright 2026)

course_use: Critical-reading exercise, compare with Allegro's Polish short-form result. Free.

title: Unlocking marketing efficiency: PwC and Analyx on budget optimisation with MMM
author_source: PwC Germany with Analyx (consultancy; client and result not verified)

author_source: Heuking Kühn Lüer Wojtek, 23 Oct 2026

author_source: IAB (US), released 20 Oct 2026, comment period to 4 Nov 2026

author_source: Alliance Digitale (France), 29 Jan 2026, 57 pp. per PPC Land

title: DoWhy
author_source: PyWhy community (origin Microsoft Research); MIT; version 0.14 (8 Nov 2025); about 8,400 GitHub stars
note: [Open source] General causal inference library built around explicit graphs, identification and refutation tests. Not an MMM tool. Use it to teach the identification logic behind MMM controls, such as why seasonality and country demand are confounders of spend.
course_use: Background and methods lab for advanced students. Free.

title: Prophetverse
author_source: Felipe Angelim Vieira; Apache-2.0; version 0.12.0 (19 Mar 2026); built on sktime and NumPyro
note: [Open source] Generalised Prophet that also covers marketing mix modelling with custom priors and non-linear effects. A fourth modelling route students rarely meet, with a forecasting-first design. Check the documentation for geo panels before assigning it.
course_use: Optional project tool. Free.

title: EconML
author_source: PyWhy community (origin Microsoft Research); MIT; version 0.17.0 (PyPI 31 Jul 2026)
note: [Open source] Heterogeneous treatment effect estimators such as double machine learning. Relevant to whether a media effect varies by country characteristics, a question MMM partial pooling only approximates.
course_use: Advanced project option. Free.

title: Meridian MLflow demo and JAX calibration notebooks
author_source: Google; Apache-2.0; files in the demo folder of google/meridian on 9 Nov 2026; follow package version 2.2.0
note: [Open source] Hosted and MLOps route not covered in the earlier guide: the demo folder has an MLflow tracking notebook and Meridian_Prior_Calibration_JAX. Google recommends a GPU runtime, and budget optimisation in Colab needs one. No Google document describing a Vertex AI training or pipeline setup was found on 9 Nov 2026, so use Colab or Meridian Studio in class and treat agency Vertex recipes with care. Cortex for Meridian appears in Google Cloud docs but its pages returned 404.
course_use: Lab for the production session, about 60 minutes. Free; Colab GPU quota may limit a class.

title: pysyncon (synthetic control in Python)
author_source: Stiofáin Fordham; MIT; version 1.7.0 (13 Sep 2026)
note: [Open source] Implements standard, robust, augmented and penalized synthetic control with placebo tests, and aims to reconcile with the R packages Synth and augsynth. Fits country-level case work: a treated country against a donor pool of other countries.
course_use: Lab on a single-country campaign. Free.

title: Trimmed Match (Google geo experiment analysis)
author_source: Google; Apache-2.0; no tagged releases; last push 1 Jun 2023 (GitHub API, 9 Nov 2026)
note: [Open source] Robust analysis of matched-pair geo experiments with heterogeneous geos, which is the normal situation across countries of very different size. Unmaintained since 2023. The sister repository matched_markets in the earlier guide is now archived, so point new work to Meridian GeoX.
course_use: Methods reading only; not for a live lab. Free.

title: mmm-eval: validation framework for MMM packages
author_source: Mutinex; Apache-2.0 per README; version 0.12.0 in pyproject; last push 28 Jul 2026; GitHub
note: [Open source] Standard tests for PyMC-Marketing and Meridian: holdout accuracy, in-sample accuracy, cross-validated holdout, refresh stability, perturbation and placebo. Rare example of a vendor releasing validation code. Mutinex also promotes it as an Open MMM Validation Framework for comparing vendors; the choice of tests is the vendor's. Python 3.11 or 3.12.
course_use: Lab: run the same country panel through both packages and compare stability. Free.

title: LightweightMMM repository (archived, deprecated)
author_source: Google; Apache-2.0; final version 0.1.9 (23 May 2023); repository archived 19 Jan 2026 per GitHub banner
note: [Open source] Status check: read-only since January 2026, and the README tells users to move to Meridian. It still has more than 1,000 GitHub stars and appears in older tutorials, so students will find it. Useful history for the hierarchical geo model that Meridian extended. Do not build new labs on it.
course_use: Background on the package lineage. Free.

title: PyMC-Marketing feature comparison with Robyn, Orbit KTR and Meridian
author_source: PyMC Labs documentation page (vendor-written; viewed 9 Nov 2026)
note: [Open source] Table of 19 attributes, including hierarchical geographic modelling (PyMC-Marketing and Meridian yes, Robyn and Orbit KTR no), lift-test calibration, GPU and MLflow support. Written by the maker of one of the packages: the claims of 2 to 20 times faster sampling and 40 percent lower error come from its own benchmark. Good exercise in reading a vendor table critically.
course_use: Reading, 10 minutes, with a critique task. Free.

title: CausalImpact (R)
author_source: Kay Brodersen, Alain Hauser, Google; Apache-2.0; version 1.4.1 on CRAN (26 Sep 2025)
note: [Open source] The standard Bayesian structural time-series package for measuring the effect of one campaign in one market against control series. Natural follow-up when a country has too few geos for a designed experiment. The earlier guide lists only Google's Python port.
course_use: Lab on staggered country launches. Free.

title: Karpiu (MMM on Orbit)
author_source: Edwin Ng; MIT; beta; last push 23 May 2024
note: [Open source] Thin MMM layer that calls Uber Orbit as the backend, showing how a time-varying coefficient model can be turned into MMM. Author labels it beta and it has been inactive since 2024.
course_use: Reference for students exploring Orbit. Free.

title: CausalML
author_source: Uber; Apache-2.0 per PyPI classifier; version 0.18.0 (12 Oct 2026)
note: [Open source] Uplift modelling and meta-learners for user-level experiments. Useful contrast: it needs individual-level data, which GDPR consent and walled gardens often remove, while MMM needs only aggregates.
course_use: Contrast case in the privacy session. Free.

title: Robyn and robynpy maintenance status (no new release since the earlier guide)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science; MIT; Robyn 3.12.1 on CRAN (2 Jul 2025); robynpy 0.3.6 on PyPI (3 Apr 2025); latest GitHub release tag v3.12.0 (19 Dec 2024); checked 9 Nov 2026
note: [Open source] Versions unchanged from the earlier guide, which is the point: no CRAN release for 16 months and no robynpy release for 19 months, and the last push to the repository was 26 Jan 2026 (GitHub API). The R DESCRIPTION on the default branch reads 3.11.1.9001, below the CRAN version. Contrast with the weekly activity at PyMC-Marketing and Meridian when discussing which package to bet a course or a company on. Robyn has no hierarchical geo pooling, so multi-country work means one model per country.
course_use: Discussion of open-source maintenance risk; install from CRAN for labs. Free.

title: Paramark mmm workbench (wrapper for lightweight_mmm)
author_source: Paramark; Apache-2.0; last push 28 Oct 2026; no version number found
note: [Open source] Wraps a forked LightweightMMM behind a config file and CSV input. A rare public view of how a commercial MMM firm scaffolds open-source code. The firm's GitHub organisation also holds forks of Robyn, Meridian, GeoLift and CausalImpact. That shows familiarity with these tools; it does not prove what runs in its product.
course_use: Case for the build versus buy session. Free.

title: CurrencyConverter (Python)
author_source: GitHub user alexprengere; Apache-2.0; version 0.18.23 (31 Oct 2026)
note: [Supporting library] Offline conversion with historical ECB rates, simple enough for a first lab on turning local-currency spend into a common currency. ECB reference coverage is limited to the currencies it publishes.
course_use: Lab on currency harmonisation. Free.

title: Databricks Media Mix Modeling solution accelerator
author_source: Databricks Industry Solutions; Databricks License (third-party libraries keep their own); last push 29 Oct 2026; no version
note: [Supporting library] Worked MLOps example: synthetic data generation, a PyMC-Marketing fit, MLflow tracking and an asset bundle job. No geo model in the README, so an obvious student extension is to add a country dimension. Licence is not a standard open-source one.
course_use: Lab or project for data-engineering students; needs a Databricks workspace. Free code.

title: MARFOR Marketing Mix Modeling (Claude plugin)
author_source: wogulgames; MIT; last push 6 Oct 2026; 2 stars
note: [Supporting library] Plugin that checks MMM data readiness, explains concepts on the user's own numbers and stress-tests budget plans across uncertainty ranges. Very new, unknown maintainer. The robustness idea, not the tool, is the reusable point.
course_use: Optional idea for a student project. Free.

title: MLflow
author_source: MLflow project, originated at Databricks; Apache-2.0; version 3.18.0 (3 Nov 2026)
note: [Supporting library] Experiment tracking that both Meridian and PyMC-Marketing support. When a team runs one model per country every month, tracking which model produced which ROI is the real problem, and this shows it clearly.
course_use: Short demo in the production session. Free.

title: Meridian agent skills
author_source: Google for Developers; distributed in google/meridian (Apache-2.0); no date shown on page
note: [Supporting library] Five official skills for coding assistants: documentation consultant, model building, result visualisation, budget optimisation and scenario planner. They pause for confirmation before column mapping, priors, long MCMC runs and script execution, a good design pattern to discuss. Confirmed in the repository skills folder on 9 Nov 2026. Announced with GeoX general availability in September 2026.
course_use: Lab: compare an assisted and a manual Meridian build. Free.

title: MixLift
author_source: Author not stated on PyPI; MIT; version 0.5.3 (15 Apr 2026, PyPI); description advertises USD 299 per month
note: [Supporting library] MCP server built on the idea of CSV in, budget recommendations out; its PyPI description advertises a USD 299 monthly price despite the MIT tag, so check what is actually free. Use as a caution: one-step budget advice without visible diagnostics is the failure mode to teach against. Not reviewed in depth.
course_use: Critique example. Free.

title: ecbdata (Python)
author_source: Luca Mingarelli; MIT; version 0.1.1 (23 Mar 2025)
note: [Supporting library] Small wrapper that queries the ECB Data Portal, returning data frames. Handy for exchange rates; low activity, so keep the direct API as fallback.
course_use: Lab helper. Free.

title: google-meridian-mcp-server (Adswerve)
author_source: Adswerve; BSD-3-Clause; last push 6 Nov 2026; no release; 2 GitHub stars
note: [Supporting library] FastMCP server with a focused set of model-analysis tools, from a certified Meridian partner. Small and new, so check test coverage before use. Compare with the BlueAlpha server to discuss how much of a model an agent should be allowed to touch.
course_use: Optional demo. Free.

title: imfp (Python client for IMF data)
author_source: Promptly Technologies; Apache-2.0 per GitHub (PyPI classifier says MIT); version 2.1.1 (22 Oct 2026)
note: [Supporting library] Downloads IMF series through the current SDMX 3.0 API, relevant because the IMF replaced its older data services. Licence metadata conflicts, so check before redistributing.
course_use: Lab helper for macro controls. Free.

title: mcp-server-meridian
author_source: BlueAlpha; MIT; version 0.2.6 (6 Apr 2026, PyPI)
note: [Supporting library] Exposes a fitted Meridian model to an LLM with more than 15 tools for ROI, saturation, adstock, prior versus posterior and budget reallocation, with a decision log. The write-up itself shows prior-dominated parameters, a good reminder that a confident chat answer may rest on priors. Vendor-written; sample results come from one demo model.
course_use: Demo in the AI and MMM session. Free.

title: pycountry
author_source: pycountry project; LGPL-2.1; version 26.2.16 (17 Feb 2026)
note: [Supporting library] ISO country, subdivision and currency codes. Simple but essential: merged multi-country panels often fail on inconsistent country names and codes.
course_use: Lab helper. Free.

title: pymc-marketing-mcp
author_source: Mamdouh Aboammar; Apache-2.0 per README (GitHub API shows no recognised licence); last push 24 Oct 2026; 3 stars
note: [Supporting library] MCP server where the agent frames the question, PyMC-Marketing computes and the server validates inputs and records provenance. Targets Python 3.12 and 3.13 and PyMC-Marketing 1.x. Its self-description as production-grade is unverified; one-person project.
course_use: Optional demo for technical students. Free.

title: sdmx1 (Python SDMX client)
author_source: SDMX Python developers (repository khaeru/sdmx); Apache-2.0; version 2.28.0 (18 Oct 2026)
note: [Supporting library] One client for SDMX data sources from statistical agencies, so the same code can reach multiple official providers. Better teaching value than one wrapper per source. Check its source list for the agency needed.
course_use: Lab: pull FX and macro controls by code. Free.

title: simba-mcp
author_source: SIMBA; MIT; version 0.18.0 (14 Oct 2026, PyPI)
note: [Supporting library] Connects assistants such as Claude and Cursor to the commercial SIMBA platform. Open connector in front of a paid product, a business model worth naming in class.
course_use: Example in the AI and MMM session. Connector free, platform paid.

title: wbgapi (World Bank API client)
author_source: GitHub user tgherzog; MIT; version 1.0.14 (27 Feb 2026)
note: [Supporting library] Python access to World Bank indicators, for example PPP factors and population for per-capita country panels.
course_use: Lab helper. Free.

title: workalendar
author_source: workalendar project; MIT; version 17.0.0 (1 Jan 2023)
note: [Supporting library] Working-day calendars by country. Useful for retail and B2B week definitions, which the python-holidays package does not directly give. No release since 2023, so check holiday rules for recent years.
course_use: Reference. Free.

title: Advertising Experiments at RestaurantGrades (spreadsheet supplement 916-702)
author_source: Harvard Business School, 2016
note: Hypothetical experiment with two treatment arms and a control group of restaurants, with spreadsheet supplement. Alternative to Star Digital for practising lift estimation. Page blocked automated reading, so authors and price were not seen.
course_use: Calibration exercise. Paid via HBP, price unknown.

title: Elysian Fertility and Surrogacy: attribution as a decision problem (three-part case)
author_source: Mohanbir Sawhney (Kellogg) and Michael Stratta (Arcalea); Harvard Business Publishing, 2025
note: Recent sequential case, USD 1.44M budget across ten digital channels for a Californian clinic with about USD 10M revenue. Parts A to C release traffic, then conversion and revenue, then ROAS, CAC and predictive data, and students revise a six-channel allocation. Uses multi-touch attribution, so it is a foil to MMM, not an MMM case. Single market. Details come from the vendor's page; HBP product number and price not stated.
course_use: Case session contrasting attribution with MMM logic. Paid via HBP, price unknown; check HBP Educator catalogue.

title: Fictitious two-channel brand and sales case with Jupyter notebook (long-term ad effectiveness)
author_source: Schlereth, Reh, Weber (WHU) with Fichtner and Mueller-Klockmann (Meta Marketing Science), Nov 2022; SSRN 4103941
note: Free teaching-ready material from a German business school: fictitious case inspired by real data comparing two ad channels on sales and brand equity in multiplicative regressions, with example data and code in a GitHub Gist (gist.github.com/WHU-Chair-of-Digital-Marketing/ee05482d39317561ac610a8f6ce72026). Not designed as a teaching case and licence is not stated. Meta co-authored, so note the interest. Fills the long-term brand gap in the open-source tools.
course_use: Lab on long-term effects, data and code included. Free; check Gist licence before redistributing.

title: Flipkart: Leveraging Customer Analytics (M-1046 / UV9185)
author_source: Ron Wilcox, Bianca Kemp, Thomas Adkins; Darden Business Publishing, 19 Mar 2025
note: 5-page field case with a student spreadsheet and an instructor PowerPoint, mainly multiple regression on individual purchase data for promotional spend. Used in Darden's required marketing course and supports comparing US and Indian shoppers. Promotion response, not MMM, but the cross-cultural discussion fits. Page: store.darden.virginia.edu/flipkart-leveraging-customer-analytics.
course_use: Warm-up regression case for an international section. Paid, USD 11.95 list on HBR Store.

title: Note on Marketing Mix Models: Evaluating Bang for the Buck (M-0339)
author_source: Paul W. Farris, Christopher Gale, James Olver; Darden, 2 Apr 1987
note: 9-page technical note on model purpose, response function types and independent versus interactive effects, evaluated in a spreadsheet. Old, but a compact pre-software introduction that lets students build a response function by hand. No adstock or Bayesian content. Price not shown on the page.
course_use: Optional historical reading in week one. Paid, price not listed; check Darden store.

title: Optimal Marketing (Samsung), Harvard Business Review article distributed as a teaching reading
author_source: Marcel Corstjens and Jeffrey Merrihue, HBR, October 2007, pp. 114-121; listed at The Case Centre
note: Best fit for cross-country allocation among published teaching readings. Samsung, about USD 1 billion yearly marketing, built predictive models over 18 months across more than 400 product-category and country combinations (a WARC summary says over 450) and used what-if testing to reallocate. 16 pages. Article rather than case, no data, teaching note not confirmed. The Case Centre blocked automated reading, details from search listings.
course_use: Reading paired with the Bayer paper for the allocation session. Paid, price unknown; WU licence (check) for HBR.

title: Star Digital: Assessing the Effectiveness of Display Advertising (M347)
author_source: Sridhar Narayanan and Taylan Yildiz; sold through HBR Store, 6 Mar 2013
note: 5 pages with an Excel file of disguised experiment data. Controlled test of display ads at a company spending over USD 100M a year. Works as the experiment leg of the calibration module: students estimate lift, then discuss how it would enter an MMM prior. Single-country and pre-MMM tooling.
course_use: Case plus data exercise for calibration. Paid, USD 11.95 list on HBR Store; educator pricing may differ.

title: WU EMCEE case collection: UNIQA vs VIG and ESET
author_source: Arnold Schuh, Ferdinand Mayrhofer; WU Competence Center for Emerging Markets and CEE (2020, 2015)
note: No MMM case exists in the collection. Useful as market context: UNIQA vs VIG contrasts a single regional brand with a multi-brand CEE strategy, which raises the question of what a pooled model should treat as one brand; ESET covers a Slovak firm going global. Both free PDFs, no modelling data. A WU MMM extension of these cases would be an original contribution.
course_use: Context reading before a CEE geo-pooling design task. Free PDF.

title: 101: Effectiveness: Marketing Mix Modelling (MMM) 2026 (ISBA)
author_source: ISBA, curated with Pete Davis, Getmemedia.com (14 Apr 2026)
note: UK advertiser association primer on MMM with attribution and testing. Member-only video and slides. Length and presenters not stated.
course_use: Only if WU has ISBA access; otherwise note as an industry training benchmark. Members only.

title: AI for Engineers: Build an AI-Powered MMM Solution with Bayesian Inference (Berlin webinar)
author_source: Berlin AI Engineering Group by m|rig (16 Jan 2026)
note: 60 minutes online. Hierarchical Bayesian MMM with priors across stores or regions in plain PyMC on the Rossmann sales dataset (German drugstore chain). Speaker not named, recording not confirmed. PRE-DATES PyMC 6 and PyMC-Marketing 1.0.
course_use: Idea source: Rossmann data as a German hierarchical lab. Free.

title: Ads DevCast E6: The What and Why on Meridian
author_source: Google Ads developer team; host Cory Liseno, guests Katie Munro and Jeff Li (28 May 2026, per PPC Land)
note: Product team explains Hill curves, adstock, why Google open-sourced the model given its conflict of interest, and the attribution, experiments and MMM feedback loop. PRE-DATES BREAKING API (Meridian 2.0, Sep 2026), but it is conceptual, so little is affected. Length could not be read from the page.
course_use: Video for the session on platform-built models. Free.

title: Advanced Funnel-Aware MMM: Geo-Level Mediation Through Lower-Funnel Spend
author_source: PyMC-Marketing documentation (stable)
note: Weekly synthetic geo panel with three regions over 130 weeks and known truth. Compares five naive specifications with a funnel model, uses a causal graph, then runs funnel-aware budget optimisation. Very long notebook, a full lab session or more. In the stable (1.x) docs; exact version watermark not confirmed. Regions are not countries, so students must relabel and rescale.
course_use: Advanced lab; simulate countries by relabelling geos. Free.

title: Build a Marketing Mix Model with Claude Code: From OLS to Bayesian (Maven workshop)
author_source: Gui Diaz-Berrio, Maven
note: One-day live workshop with certificate of completion and lifetime recordings. Requires Python 3.10+ and PyMC 5.x, so it PRE-DATES the PyMC 6 base of PyMC-Marketing 1.0. Price and dates not listed. No geo content mentioned.
course_use: Benchmark for an AI-assisted modelling lab. Paid, price not listed.

title: Building a production-ready MMM pipeline with Fivetran and PyMC-Marketing (webinar)
author_source: PyMC Labs Online Meetup; William Dean, Carlos Trujillo, Luke Alexander (23 Oct 2025)
note: About 60 minutes. Data ingestion and dbt models through to budget optimisation and scaling across markets and brands. PRE-DATES BREAKING API (PyMC-Marketing 1.0); version not stated. Page does not say whether a recording exists.
course_use: Background on the data engineering side of multi-market MMM. Free.

title: Data Analytics Methods for Marketing (Coursera, offered by Meta)
author_source: Meta, instructor Anke Audenaert, Coursera
note: About 12 hours in four modules; module 4 covers marketing mix models and attribution. Taught in English, 22 languages listed (check German). Enrolment free; shareable certificate requires purchase (price not listed; Coursera Plus shown at EUR 206 per year promotion). Introductory, no Robyn or Python version claimed on the page.
course_use: Pre-course for marketing students. Free to audit, certificate paid.

title: From Experiments to Priors: Eliciting Informative Priors for Your Marketing Mix Model
author_source: Carlos Trujillo, personal site (8 Feb 2026, updated 16 Sep 2026)
note: Long worked tutorial: CausalPy synthetic control on a spend cut, then a mapping to the saturation curve, then priors in a multidimensional MMM. PRE-DATES BREAKING API: watermark shows pymc_marketing 0.17.1, PyMC 5.28.5. Concept still valid; code needs the 1.0 migration guides.
course_use: Advanced reading on calibration; code as an upgrade exercise. Free.

title: Fundamentals of Marketing Mix Modeling (Udemy)
author_source: Udemy (instructor not confirmed)
note: About 5 h 52 min, 86 lectures, last updated March 2026, 4.4 from 71 ratings, 351 students (search snippet). Tools and price could not be read because the page blocks automated access. Updated before PyMC-Marketing 1.0 and Meridian 2.0.
course_use: Optional self-study. Paid, price not confirmed.

title: MMM Case Study II: Funnel-Aware Modeling, ROAS Calibration, and Budget Planning
author_source: PyMC-Marketing documentation (stable)
note: Follow-on to the end-to-end case study. Public weekly data of 209 weeks, paid search as a mediator, experiment ROAS ranges (hypothetical), time-slice cross-validation. National only. In the stable (1.x) docs; exact version watermark not confirmed.
course_use: Lab after the first case study. Free.

title: MMM: EEMEA Local Webinars (Poland, Romania, Türkiye, CZ/SK)
author_source: NielsenIQ (published 26 Aug 2026)
note: On-demand vendor webinars per market on incrementality, ROI, budget optimisation and retail media in Central and Eastern Europe. Rare country-specific material for the region around Vienna. Language, length and speakers not stated; proprietary method, not open source.
course_use: Background on CEE markets. Free, registration may apply.

title: Marketing Mix Modeling Essentials: Virtual 2-Hr Burst (ANA School of Marketing)
author_source: Dr. Jose Mendoza, NYU School of Professional Studies, for ANA
note: 120-minute non-coding workshop agenda: what MMM is, making sense of data, interpreting and communicating results, AI. Session code suggests September 2026; this date has passed. Price not listed. Useful as a template for a manager-level unit.
course_use: Benchmark for a non-technical teaching unit. Paid, price not listed.

title: Marketing Mix Modeling path (Vexpower)
author_source: Mike Taylor, Vexpower
note: 18 weekly simulator-based courses: 7 in Excel or Google Sheets, then Robyn, LightweightMMM, Orbit, log-log, geo-level MMM (week 12), Bayesian MMM. USD 35 per month for the whole library; weeks 1, 8, 9, 10 marked free. No certificate mentioned. Path page does not list Meridian or PyMC-Marketing, so check for currency. Good non-coder route.
course_use: Self-study or pre-course for non-programmers. Paid, about USD 35 per month, some weeks free.

title: Marketing Science Bootcamp: MMM, Attribution & Incrementality (Maven)
author_source: Gui Diaz-Berrio, Maven
note: Live cohort: search listing says 4 weeks, 8 live sessions, 53 lessons, 6 projects; page FAQ says 6 to 10 hours per week with two 90-minute sessions. Meridian on multi-geo data, PyMC, geo-experiments, Claude Code skills. Certificate of completion. No software versions given, base price and next start date not listed (early-bird code dated June 2026). Multi-country not mentioned.
course_use: Benchmark for course design; further study for strong students. Paid, price not listed.

title: Marketing-Mix-Modeling (University of Zurich lecture, German)
author_source: University of Zurich, Chair for Marketing and Market Research; Selin Akca
note: Only German-language university MMM course found in DACH. 3 ECTS. Pricing regression, choice-based conjoint, structural equation models for marketing-mix endogeneity. Page dates from 2019 and is inconsistent about the semester; no open-source MMM software named. Check whether it still runs.
course_use: Syllabus comparison for the WU course. Free page; course for UZH students.

title: PyMC Labs workshops and Bayesian Marketing Analytics cohort
author_source: PyMC Labs
note: Beginner to advanced workshops on enquiry. A preview version of the PyMC Labs site also describes open cohorts of 8 live online sessions, including Bayesian Marketing Analytics, and custom corporate workshops. No prices or dates found. Treat the cohort detail as unconfirmed until seen on the live site.
course_use: Option for instructor training or a sponsored workshop. Paid, quote on request.

title: mmm-geo-toy-meridian: reproducible geo MMM pipeline on Meridian 2.1.0
author_source: GitHub user fraschen (name not given)
note: One of the few public projects found on Meridian 2.x. Pins google-meridian 2.1.0 with JAX. Google's simulated data with 40 geos, 156 weeks, five channels. Scripts for EDA, fit, holdout, acceptance gates, scenarios, in a container. Candid result: useful for direction, not for decisions, since the 13-week forecast check failed. No notebooks, no licence stated for the repo, geos are not countries.
course_use: Project template; example of honest acceptance criteria. Free; check licence before reuse.

title: mmm-meridian-vs-pymc: same simulated data in both libraries
author_source: GitHub user yc4379-commits (name not given)
note: Simulated dating-app revenue across 10 US DMAs over 104 weeks, five channels, known truth and a lift test, with a Streamlit dashboard. Versions sit in requirements files that were not read, so check them against PyMC-Marketing 1.0 and Meridian 2.0 before use. Needs two virtual environments because the libraries want different ArviZ versions. US only, no currency handling, no licence stated.
course_use: Comparison lab or project starting point. Free; check licence before reuse.

title: MMM API Migration Guide (legacy MMM class to the multidimensional MMM)
author_source: PyMC-Marketing documentation
note: Side-by-side code for imports, the explicit build_model step, the intercept rename, the mmm.plot namespace, the sensitivity sweep and the BudgetOptimizerWrapper with xarray bounds. Rendered with pymc_marketing 1.0.0.dev0. Does not cover geo or country dims. Caveat: its quick-reference table on default pooling appears to contradict its own section 2, so check defaults before teaching them.
course_use: Lab handout for adapting any pre-1.0 tutorial. Free.

title: MMM Dims Migration Guide (pymc.dims and geo-varying priors)
author_source: PyMC-Marketing documentation
note: Key trap for multi-country models: a raw array passed as a prior parameter is matched to the rightmost dim, so with dims=(geo, channel) a 1D array is read as varying by channel. To vary by country it must be wrapped in a DataArray with dims=geo. Built against pymc_marketing 1.0.0.dev0, PyMC 6.0.1, ArviZ 1.2.0.
course_use: Lab: specifying country-level priors correctly. Free.

title: Meridian GitHub Discussion #672: Using a global posterior as prior for local (country) models
author_source: Google Meridian maintainers and users
note: A practitioner with several countries needs separate country models but finds them unstable for low-data channels. Accepted answer (21 May 2025): marginal posteriors from a global multi-geo model can inform country priors, but Meridian priors are independent so the joint posterior is not carried over. Compact real example of the pooled versus local decision. Pre-2.0, but the logic still applies.
course_use: Discussion case on global versus local modelling. Free.

title: Meridian InputData API reference: currency_code
author_source: Google for Developers
note: Only official multi-currency hook found. currency_code (added in 2.0) is an optional ISO 4217 code for all monetary values in the dataset; if unset, reports default to the dollar sign. One code per dataset, and the page says nothing about mixed currencies or conversion. Inference, not stated by Google: a multi-country model needs spend and revenue converted to one currency before loading, and the FX choice is the analyst's.
course_use: Lab on preparing multi-currency panels; pair with ECB and PPP data. Free.

title: Meridian v2.2.0 release (5 Nov 2026)
